items.text: Typed delta schema + deterministic Curator for playbook edits. A delta is `{ target, anchor, operation: add|revise|retire, body, provenance, evidenceRef }`. The Curator merges deltas by anchor with NO model in the merge path — this determinism is ACE's load-bearing property and what prevents context collapse. Wholesale rewriting of a playbook section becomes a lint error. `provenance` reuses the tagging vocabulary already defined in `compaction-strategy.md` (`[owner:<name> <date>]` / `[self-imposed]` / `[peer:<sid>]` / `[inferred]`), so an agent-authored delta can never be promoted to an owner directive by a later re-read.

Wholesale rewriting of a playbook section becomes a lint error. `provenance` reuses the tagging vocabulary already defined in `compaction-strategy.md` (`[owner:<name> <date>]` / `[self-imposed]` / `[peer:<sid>]` / `[inferred]`), so an agent-authored delta can never be promoted to an owner directive by a later re-read. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high

items.text: Reflector: mine execution feedback into CANDIDATE deltas. Sources all already exist — work-item completion evidence, `improvements:capture` observation lane, gate verdicts, EI filings, coord escalations. Output is typed deltas for the Curator, never prose. Runs on the existing routine/loop infrastructure (this is the sleep-time-compute pattern: offline work between wakes, where per the paper the payoff scales with query predictability — and agent-wake queries are highly predictable). Candidate deltas are proposals; P-002's budget is the gate that forces a retirement to pay for each addition.

Never leave a live limit-carrying session with null context_tokens.

items.text: Make a work-item HAND-OFF verifiable, and make the safe remedy discoverable without reading a hint. Measured 2026-08-24: a leader push-assigned WI-41117 to a live, blocked peer via work_items:claim { assignee: <peer> } and got claim_conflict with holder = ITSELF, refused by an admission/trust gate — AFTER it had already told that peer 'I am assigning it to you now'. Had the result not been read, the peer would have waited indefinitely on an assignment that never lands while believing it was unblocked, which is worse than being told no. Two fixes: (a) a hand-off that cannot complete should fail in terms the caller will act on; (b) the correct remedy is counter-intuitive and currently only reachable via the result hint — do NOT work_items:release to hand over, because release clears the assignee and opens the item to the WHOLE fleet, so a self-selecting peer can beat the intended recipient to it. Keeping an item pinned to the WRONG holder is a safer race than briefly unowning it. That asymmetry deserves a first-class transfer verb rather than a hint.

items.text: Standing facts need an EXPIRY, a PROBE, and a FALSIFIER — adjacent to P-017, which narrows to coord:orient folding facts VERBATIM into every wake. That verbatim fold is precisely what makes a WRONG fact more dangerous than a wrong carry-note: a carry-note is rewritten every wake, whereas a fact is re-injected unchanged forever and never re-verified, because not having to re-derive it IS its value proposition. Measured 2026-08-24: the standing fact carry-note-lives-under-sb-devboard-hive-not-papercusp asserted the wrong harness and was phrased imperatively — 'OPERATIVE: DO NOT COMPLY by writing loop:checkpoint with harness:papercusp' — so an agent obeyed it and silently routed five checkpoints into an unread store across an entire incident. It carried no probe and no expiry, so nothing could ever have caught it; it was falsified only when a wake happened to report which store it had actually read. FIX: require or strongly prompt for a re-check probe on facts:assert, the way loop:checkpoint checks[] already do, and render a fact's age at fold time so a reader can weigh it.

items.text: Supersede cascade: when a plan is superseded or consolidated (plans:set-plan-status superseded, or a consolidation Decision), find every non-terminal item in other plans whose deliverable is shipping or accepting that plan (a "Ship <slug>" carrier). Park it out of claim_next with a pointer to the superseding decision, notify its holder, and raise a repair obligation on the carrier plan. Guard (Vitest): superseding plan X parks a todo/wip item in plan Y that carries X, and leaves unrelated items claimable. items.text: Decision-first cross-lane rulings [owner:Avi 2026-07-26]. During the fleet run a leader ruling was recorded via `plans:add-decision`; a member later RE-READ it, found its own earlier mapping wrong on 2 of 3 sites, self-corrected, and swept up 5 more — precisely because the ruling was re-readable and auditable rather than a message that had scrolled away. Make this the default: (a) document in the su playbook + repo `CLAUDE.md` that a ruling other lanes must follow is recorded as a plan decision AT THE MOMENT IT FORMS, never only in coord; (b) surface a plan's decisions at CLAIM time (in the claim/`get_next` payload or the plan-item brief) so a member sees governing decisions without being told to look; (c) make coord relay cheap — when a leader broadcasts a ruling, include the decision ref so recipients can re-read the authority rather than trusting the paraphrase.  — note: ← WI-6160 completed (done)

A leader mid-execution on a blocked item kept working after it unblocked; a member's claim-spec auto-claimed it within seconds; the collision surfaced only at close time via `claim_conflict`, after the duplicated-work window. Holding the linked WORK-ITEM is not holding the PLAN item — an easy and costly conflation. Either (a) notify the holder of a linked work-item when its plan item is claimed by someone else, or (b) surface the plan-item holder in `work_items:get` so an agent mid-execution can see the item is not theirs.  — note: ← WI-6164 completed (done)

items.text: **Spike + GATE: is Arrow actually worth it on OUR data?** Take the real `plans.items` result (1.67MB) and `workItems.byHarness`, encode as Arrow IPC, and measure end-to-end against the JSON baseline already recorded: stringify 15.6ms + base64 14.2ms + TextDecoder 5.1ms + JSON.parse 20.1ms = 55.1ms per 6.65MB. Measure BOTH legs: server-side Arrow encode cost, and V8-side read cost through `apache-arrow`. GATE: if the total does not beat JSON by a wide margin on real (not synthetic) rows, STOP and close this plan — our rows are wide and string-heavy, which is Arrow's weakest case, and that must be disproved with data before any of P-002..P-004 is written.  — note: GATE RAN, GATE FAILED. Arrow LOSES by +20.9ms net on real data. See D-003.

items.text: **GATE CHECK before any Phase 2 work — do not skip.** Re-measure the wave AFTER the fat projections are slimmed and the batcher is gone (plan drop-sync-batcher-2026-07-25). items.text: Canary routine should create F-CANARY with HIGH priority. hive-canary-action.ts queues the daily canary with no priority/rank, so in a deep hive frontier (observed todo_depth 214) the ranker places higher-ranked features first and the deadline-bound canary (deadlineHours:6) can sit unplaced for hours — a latent reason the canary lags even when the loop is healthy. Fix: set a high backlog priority (low feature_order) when creating F-CANARY-<date> so the health canary is always placed promptly. (Worked around this session by manually boosting F-CANARY-20260628/27 to priority 0/1.) (hive-canary-action.ts now inserts F-CANARY with feature_order default 0 = top; configurable via payload.featureOrder. Unit tests 9/9 green. Deploys via pipeline.)

items.text: DURABLE FIX — de-starve the Queen↔Scout review under bee-cap saturation. ROOT: plan-review is a PURELY idle-gated activity (owner-steering.ts IDLE_ACTIVITY_KINDS) while the Scout fires on friction-OR-idle, so under chronic saturation the Queen never reviews routed drafts. Smallest fix: either (a) guarantee plan-review a small slice each Queen wake regardless of idle ratio, OR (b) deadline-escalate a scout-routed draft unreviewed >N hours (mirror the canary deadline) so drafts cannot starve silently. Investigate the Queen wake loop + plan-review scheduling; land with tests.  (Delegated implementation to a focused subagent de-starve plan-review under saturation, additive + kill-switchable + tested.) (Landed: scout/draft-review-watchdog.ts — deadline→friction-wake backstop default 12h, env PAPERCUSP_SCOUT_DRAFT_REVIEW_STALE_SEC, <=0 kill switch, wired into routinesTick; 27 tests green, tsc clean. Wakes the live Queen about stale scout drafts never ratifies/deprecates. Deploys via pipeline.) (← WI-965 completed)

items.text: Queen wake-handling must DISPOSE scout-routed drafts when woken — the SECOND half of link 5 (P-002 only delivers the wake). EVIDENCE: even after a targeted hive:wake nudge to review scout-rubric-hive-coordination-health-scorecard-2026-06-26, the Queen left it draft/v1 (~20min) — so a friction-wake is necessary but NOT sufficient; the Queen's prompt/logic doesn't prioritize disposing scout drafts (promote=ready / iterate-with-feedback / deprecate-with-learnings). RECOMMENDED DEFAULT (additive, bounded): add Queen role guidance — on a wake carrying source='scout-draft-review' (and while any routed draft is pending), dispose each pending scout draft before returning to frontier placement, capped to a small per-wake budget so it never blocks shipping. NOTE: rubric proposals need templateData filled on ratification — the Queen must know how to ratify a RUBRIC, not just plain plan drafts. OWNER TRADE-OFF: how much Queen attention should scout-review claim vs frontier shipping? Must be live-verified post-deploy. Likely composes with queen-scout-feedback-loop-2026-06-20.  (Owner greenlit. Implementing the additive Queen wake-prompt guidance dispose scout drafts on a scout-draft-review wake, capped ~1-2/wake via a subagent; composes with the shipped P-002 wake.) (Added 'Scout-Routed Draft Review' disposal section to blueprints/base/prompts/queen.base.md shared Queen persona. LIVE on next wake PAPERCUSP_INTEGRATION_ROOT points at this tree — no deploy/re-seed. 85 prompt tests green. Composes with the P-002 scout-draft-review wake.) (← WI-973 completed)

items.text: W1.3 — DONE + TESTED + LIVE-VERIFIED (2026-07-03): mcp-proxy stale-keep-alive-socket bug. The proxy forwarded via Node's global agent (keepAlive:true) and REUSED pooled sockets to the :3070 cluster; a socket the server/worker was concurrently closing (61s keepalive + worker recycle) made a forwarded request land on a half-closed socket -> :3070 returned a spurious `400 Bad Request` (connection:close, empty body) which the proxy passed to the agent as a tool error. MEASURED ~13% failure on reuse-prone traffic (direct :3070 was clean). Fix: dedicated UPSTREAM_AGENT keepAlive:false (fresh socket per forward) in apps/operator/lib/mcp-proxy/proxy.ts + no-reuse regression test (7 proxy tests green). Live-verified: 160/160 probes 200 post-fix (was ~13% 400). Likely THE dominant source of transient tool-call failures since all agents route through the proxy. Follow-up (scale): bounded keepAlive + short keepAliveMsecs + retry-once-on-reset for thousands-of-agents throughput.

items.text: **Build the equivalence harness (the method for ask 3).** For a candidate (bash_pattern -> tool) pair: sample N=20 REAL commands from the audit corpus, express each through the proposed tool, and record whether the tool answers the SAME question — not whether it is nominally related. Verdict per pair: `equivalent` / `needs-widening` (naming the specific failing cases) / `not-a-substitute`. Land it as a committed test so it re-runs and cannot silently rot. Every P-005..P-010 verdict must cite its sample and its failures.  — note: Harness landed: packages/operator-core/lib/bash-substitution/{atomize,types,equivalence,corpus}.ts + equivalence.test.ts (30 tests green). Verdict is DERIVED from frozen real-command samples, never hand-asserted; each pair declares expectedVerdict so widening a tool without re-recording fails the test.

items.text: Equivalence audit — **git-read family**: `git status`/`log`/`diff`/`show`/`rev-parse`/`merge-base` (1,343 calls, 77 sessions) -> `capability:git` (8 uses) / `dev:pipeline_position` (48 uses). Determine which git reads are genuinely tool-shaped (is-my-edit-live -> `dev:pipeline_position`) versus genuinely raw (ad-hoc `git log -S`), and set the pattern boundary accordingly. Do NOT over-claim: this family may be largely legitimate bash. — note: EQUIVALENT (24/24, 2,387 atoms / 77 of 86 sessions) — the largest pair in the registry. D-011: the plan's premise didn't survive the tool. capability:git is an argv PASS-THROUGH ({args:string[], cwd?}, no shell), so the boundary is not tool-shaped-vs-raw but LITERAL vs SHELL-PRODUCED argv: 96.0% of reads are literal, 4.0% carry $(..)/$VAR and are excluded. Verified live (quoted multi-word --format/--since round-trip; cwd reaches a sibling worktree). ONE pattern, not two — dev:pipeline_position is the better answer for is-my-edit-live but a second row would double-fire, so it's routed inside the advisory. TIER CAVEAT: equivalent PERMITS advise but must not auto-promote — unlike every other equivalent pair this offers the SAME answer, and its gating benefit is role-dependent.

items.text: Tune the loop-pressure load-shed gate so heavy background ticks actually shed during the chronic-ELEVATED regime. items.text: Make git-sync RESUMABLE + reaper-legible so a transient event-loop stall (P-005's root) can't silently strand code. ROOT (2026-06-30 6h strand): git-sync's handleGitSync runs as ONE opaque long DBOS step (dbos/routines-workflow.ts:121) that records NO operation_output until it fully completes (commit→submodule→pointer-bump→push). When the executor stalls (GC) or a `git push` hangs, the fire has no output + no live queue row, so the executor-reaper (dbos/dbos-executor-reaper.ts:156-168) cancels it as a dead/orphaned executor + requeues → it LOOPS, never commits, silently (last_error captured: 'routineFire produced no DBOS operation output; executor reaper cancelled the stuck fire and requeued'). FIX (defense-in-depth — does NOT replace fixing the leak in P-005; it bounds the blast radius so a future stall recovers in minutes, not strands for hours): (1) Split handleGitSync into checkpointed DBOS.runStep sub-steps (eligibility → stage+content-guard → commit → submodule-commit → pointer-bump → push); each records an operation_output, so a stalled/reaped fire RESUMES from the last checkpoint instead of redoing from scratch, AND the reaper sees genuine progress instead of false-positive 'dead'. HARD CONSTRAINT: git steps have side effects — each MUST be replay-safe/idempotent (a replayed commit must NOT double-commit; guard on 'is the tree already at the expected state / has this range already been committed'). (2) Bound every git subprocess, esp. network push/fetch, with an explicit timeout so a hang fails FAST with a recorded last_error (watchdog-visible) instead of a silent reap. (3) Record a `fire_started_at` breadcrumb at the top of the fire + increment a `reaped_count` when the reaper cancels a git-sync fire, so persistent reaping is a durable, queryable signal (feeds the git-sync-stall-watchdog already shipped). Files: dbos/routines-workflow.ts, harness/git-sync/git-sync-action.ts, harness/git-sync/run-git-sync.ts, dbos/dbos-executor-reaper.ts. AC: an integration test that simulates a reap mid-git-sync-fire asserts RESUME+commit (not loop) OR fail-fast-with-recorded-error; a replay does NOT double-commit; the watchdog alarms on a synthetic persistent-reap. RELATED (already shipped, do not duplicate): git-sync-stall-watchdog + severe-event-broadcast = the DETECTION half (alarms + fleet broadcast when git-sync fires-but-doesn't-commit); THIS item is the root-hardening half.   (WI-1416 done: git-sync split into checkpointed replay-safe DBOS sub-steps eligibility→submodules→pointer-bump→push→record, bounded git subprocesses 4m net/6m local, env-tunable, fire_started_at + reaped_count breadcrumbs watchdog persistentReap verdict, reaper fast-orphan path corrected ENQUEUED-only + 10-min window; PENDING-no-queue-row is the NORMAL executing state. 1008 unit + 6 acceptance + 29 integration green.) (← WI-1416 completed)

items.text: [F-H, from the owner's 2026-07-28 question; design settled in D-012] Build the PRESENCE-TRANSITION EMITTER — the missing feeder for the mid-turn coord rail. MEASURED gap: automatic injection carries ZERO presence/liveness (turn-start-memory.ts:105 injects only the CTRL:transition delta + the mem0 block), and every coord_event_log writer is an explicit agent action (coord:send, coord:escalate), so a peer dying, going suspect, or dropping a lock emits NOTHING. The transport is already built and ratified by D-002 — mid-turn [coord+N] delivery, watermark/cursor dedup, one compressed line per delta — so this is an emitter, NOT a new channel, fold, or budget. HARD CONSTRAINT from D-012: emit ONLY when the transition intersects the RECEIVING agent's own commitments (a lock they are blocked on, an item/event they are awaiting, a leader/peer with an unanswered directed message). NEVER a roster broadcast — a standing presence fold is REJECTED (it would recreate this plan's own Phase 8 unbudgeted-channel defect, duplicate coord:orient, and be pure noise in a solo session). Being commitment-scoped is what makes it self-budgeting: silent when nothing relevant changed. Acceptance: a peer transition that intersects a blocked agent's commitment reaches it MID-TURN without a poll, and an unrelated transition produces no line at all. Filed as EI-18872678095307319. — note: ← WI-6820 completed (done)

items.text: [F-I, owner-prompted 2026-07-28] DECIDE whether assistant THINKING SUMMARIES become an input to the injection query — and if so, on which port ONLY. Owner asked (2026-07-28, while another agent was enabling thinking summaries) whether they would be picked up by the auto-injection machinery. VERIFIED ANSWER: NO, on both sides, and not by accident — (a) `lastUserContext` (injection.ts:792) filters `m.role === 'user'`, so assistant content cannot reach the recall query by construction; (b) the turn-start push path takes its query from the UserPromptSubmit hook, which posts the submitted USER prompt and fires before any assistant turn exists; (c) zero thinking/reasoning references anywhere in packages/operator-core/lib/memory/. On the WRITE side, session-extraction-llm.ts does read assistant turns but as `{role, content:string}`, and thinking is a separate content-block type — invisible there too unless someone explicitly folds thinking into assistant `content`. (Red herring for the next reader: `grep thinking` hits adv-roster.ts / transcript-search-warmup.ts — that is the roster's live-thinking presence dot, driven by transcript mtime, a display concern unrelated to memory.) RECOMMENDATION, to be ratified not assumed: do NOT feed thinking into the TURN-START query. PROMPT_QUERY_CLAMP is 1,000 chars, thinking summaries are long, and they would crowd the user's actual question out of the clamp; worse, the query becomes self-referential — the agent recalls memories about its own narration rather than the ask, diluting exactly the single globally-comparable ranked query F-C built (D-011). BUT the question points at a real gap that belongs to THIS phase: ten tool calls into a turn, the original prompt is a poor description of what the agent is now doing, and thinking is the best available signal of that. So the honest shape is: thinking as a candidate query source for the MID-TURN port specifically, never for turn-start. Sequence after the Phase 7 transport lands (D-002: ride the coord rail); measure against P-038's window before defaulting it on. — note: Ratified in D-040 — no code change needed; the correct behaviour was already in place on both ports. D-040 supersedes this item's "mid-turn candidate" phrasing: P-043 landed since, making thinking a P-047 prose question, never an addition to the identifier allowlist.

The advisory channel outspends the entire memory budget by ~2x while being subject to no budget at all.

items.text: Give the advisory channel the coord rail's cursor semantics: say it once, advance a watermark, never repeat verbatim within a session. Owner's framing 2026-07-28 — the coord system's `id > cursor` over coord_event_log is exactly the missing primitive. NON-OBVIOUS SECOND BENEFIT, and the reason to prefer routing through coord over a local seen-set: there is currently NO RECORD of what an agent was told. When an agent does the wrong thing you cannot ask "did the guard warn it, and when?" Routing advisories through coord converts them from fire-and-forget noise into an auditable delivery ledger that is queryable after the fact.  — note: DONE + LIVE-VERIFIED fleet-wide as the D-030 hybrid (ledger arm re-routed by D-031). Both arms landed in apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/pretooluse-bash-resource-gate.sh:57-256; deployed copy byte-identical (cmp, 2026-08-01). Evidence: 37 sessions carry a seen-set, 244 advisory-class claims, SIGPIPE claimed in 36/37 — see rationale.

items.text: SCOPE BOUNDARY — what should NOT move to coord, recorded so a later agent does not over-apply this. (a) The CTRL:transition block (mode/loop/route/scope): coord's contract explicitly permits ignoring a line that does not bear on your task, and a missed AUTO-mode or route transition is NOT tolerable — it must land at the very next prompt boundary, which is why turn-start-memory.ts evaluates it even for a sub-floor prompt. Moving it to coord would make it weaker. (b) turn-provenance: a classification OF the current prompt, not an async delta — it has to be inline. (c) The turn-start memory block itself stays at turn-start, because it answers the prompt; Phase 7 ADDS a mid-turn coord leg rather than relocating it. — note: RECORD-ONLY item — being written into the plan IS the deliverable; there is no build step. items.text: AUDIT-QUALITY OBSERVATION, recorded because it judges this plan's own provenance rather than its subject. Of the last four phases, THREE originated in owner questions rather than in the audit: Phase 7 (mid-turn injection) from "that includes every tool call, right?"; D-002's coord-rail mechanism from "why not ride that?"; Phase 8 (the unbudgeted advisory channel) from "anything else better suited to coord?". The audit examined the channel it was pointed at and did not enumerate the OTHER channels writing into agent context — and the largest one by volume (hook advisories, ~2x the entire memory budget) was found only because the owner asked a widening question. The methodological lesson for the next audit of any injection/budget system: START by enumerating every writer into the shared resource and measuring each one's volume, BEFORE analysing the one you were sent to look at. An audit scoped to the named component will systematically miss the unnamed ones, and the unnamed ones are where the unbudgeted spend lives. — note: RECORD-ONLY item — being written into the plan IS the deliverable; there is no build step. Closed 2026-08-02 so the actionable list reflects real remaining work.

items.text: [I-C] Determine WHICH leg saturates the limit under hybrid `floored-union`: the FP-floored cosine leg or the lexical leg admitting independently on minLexScore up to `lexicalDepth` (default 3x limit). This decides whether the fix is in the fusion mode, the lexical bar, or the limit semantics. Do not change a constant before this is answered.  — note: ANSWERED (D-008): the LEXICAL leg saturates. In floored-union (the production default; configure.ts:662 sets no fusionMode) the lexical leg admits independently at minLexScore and fusion returns slice(0,limit) — the cosine leg's 0.45 floor is bypassed by design, and the line-213 early-return is cosine-gated-mode only, so it never fires in prod. F-B must change the fusion/admission contract; tightening the cosine floor cannot move the outcome. No constant changed, as the item required.

items.text: [F-B, the core fix] Make the limit a CEILING, not a target: the push path must be able to return FEWER than K, including ZERO. Any design that sizes the injected block by a limit rather than by relevance reproduces D-005 exactly. Acceptance: the turn-start hit_count distribution stops being 97% saturated at the limit sums and starts resembling the pull path's decaying curve; zero-hit rate rises from 0.0% toward something in the pull path's range (29.2%). Measured via I-A.  — note: IMPLEMENTED + unit-verified (D-010). Push path now passes fusionMode:'cosine-gated' on all three pools, so candidates are seeded only from cosine hits and the per-pool limit becomes a CEILING (0..K) instead of a target. No constant retuned — per D-008 the cosine floor was never the problem. Rides an already-tested path (hybrid-backend.test.ts:286 pins per-call override + empty cosine -> []). 102 tests green (47 operator-core + 55 generic/memory), lint:tsc 0 errors. Revert lever: PAPERCUSP_MEMORY_FUSION_MODE=floored-union. ACCEPTANCE IS NOT CLAIMED — it is distributional and needs deployed telemetry + a data window; tracked as P-038.

That requires (a) the P-026 per-pool telemetry DEPLOYED — it is server-side with no hot reload — and (b) a data window of rows with pools IS NOT NULL. PROCEDURE: readRecallHealthByPool(sql, { surface: 'turn-start' }) and read saturationRate + zeroHitRate PER POOL (never the blended surface aggregate, which is what hid the defect originally). EXPECT: saturationRate falls well below 1.0 and zeroHitRate rises off 0.0. IF zeroHitRate overshoots far past ~29%, the 0.45 cosine floor is itself mis-calibrated for this corpus — re-tune it THEN, with telemetry in hand, and beware the fused-vs-cosine scale confusion that produced the retracted D-001. REVERT LEVER if it regresses: PAPERCUSP_MEMORY_FUSION_MODE=floored-union restores the old behaviour without a code change.  — note: MEASURED and answered — recorded in full as D-035. F-B's ceiling is deployed and WORKS (orient shows 8.2% zeros on the same code path); the residual saturation is a MISSING HARNESS SCOPE, not a fusion failure. 70.8% of turn-start and 44.8% of mid-turn recalls query the harness+hive pools with ZERO scopes, and the user pool then fills all 12 slots (correlation within 0.2pp). Fixed the unfixed mid-turn half.

items.text: [I-F, GATE — DO FIRST] Instrument the QUERY, not just the result. `memory_recall_stats` records what came BACK but never what was ASKED — no query column, no length, no origin. So the size of this defect is currently unmeasurable and no fix below can be shown to have worked. Record the query's SHAPE on the recall row (length, token count, a hash for dedup, and an origin classification — human-typed vs machine-injected, which the ⟦turn-provenance⟧ stamp already establishes for free). Then quantify over a live window: what fraction of `turn-start` queries are machine boilerplate, under N chars, or byte-identical to the previous turn's. Everything below is measured THROUGH this, exactly as I-A was for Phase 10.  — note: GATE CLEARED — instrument landed (mig 706, describeRecallQuery/readRecallQueryHealth) AND the live quantification is run and recorded as D-033. Headline: turn-start is 74.4% machine-injected, 70.0% TRUNCATED at the 1000-char clamp (251 of 254 clamped rows machine), median query length == the clamp exactly, 15.0% byte-identical repeats. Surfaced P-048 as the dominant fix.

items.text: [F-K] Populate agent signals from ACTIONS, not PROSE. v1 sources in preference order: (a) the claimed work-item / plan-item title+body — already structured, already scoped to the agent's real task, and free; (b) the recent tool-call trajectory — file paths touched, work-item/EI ids, symbol names; (c) the active file. EXPLICITLY EXCLUDE the agent's own prose and thinking summaries from v1. That exclusion is the whole design point, not timidity: prose is what creates the self-confirmation loop (the agent asserts X, retrieval returns X, the agent asserts more X), whereas actions are grounded in verifiable events the agent cannot talk itself into. The two are cleanly separable, so v1 takes the half that carries no such risk.   — note: ← WI-6644 completed (done)

items.text: [F-L] Route agent signals to the LEXICAL leg, not the cosine leg. Agent-side context is overwhelmingly IDENTIFIERS (paths, ids, symbol names) — precisely what the lexical leg exists for and what cosine embedding is worst at — and the lexical leg is EMBED-FREE, so this rides the per-turn critical path at ~zero marginal cost (the cosine leg is the embed-bound one; hybrid already overlaps them). User text keeps the cosine leg, so paraphrase recall is untouched. ⚠ D-014 COMPLIANCE, read it before writing code: this ADDS to a leg's QUERY, it never re-ranks or reorders a leg's OUTPUT — anything that reorders a fusion leg rewrites the fusion INPUT, which is the exact trap F-D caught.   — note: ← WI-6970 completed (done)

items.text: [ACCEPTANCE] Measure on the retrieval BENCH (`libs/generic/memory/src/bench`, MRR), NEVER on top_score. ⚠ THIS IS THE TRAP F-F EXPOSED AND IT IS WHY THIS DEFECT SURVIVED: the push path's score is post-fusion RRF, a RANK statistic — SOMETHING is always rank 1 — so an RRF top_score is bit-for-bit identical for a perfect query and for the literal word "continue". Measured live, `turn-start` median top_score is 0.03202 against the 2/61 = 0.032787 ceiling: 97.7% of maximum, which reads as flawless retrieval and is entirely uninformative about query quality. Report the exact-identifier and paraphrase MRR splits SEPARATELY, as the D-007 lexWeight sweep did — an identifier-heavy agent signal is expected to move those two in opposite directions, and a single blended MRR would hide the trade.   — note: D-051. Bench-measured (MRR, never top_score), splits reported separately. The PREDICTED exact-id↔paraphrase trade did NOT materialize: exact-identifier sat at ceiling 1.0000 (unmovable, a ceiling effect not underpower) while lexical-gap rose +0.1262 [0.0604,0.2054] — the identifier-heavy signal cost nothing on either. Split repairs dilution at every dose≥1 in every class (dose-3 lexical-gap +0.2904) but only ~70-76% of the loss: NOT "dilution solved". Null control exactly 0. Verification green: leg-split-arms.test.ts 10/10, lint:tsc --files clean.

items.text: [F-N, the DOMINANT query-side fix — surfaced by D-033's measurement, and larger than P-006] Stop embedding wake chrome. `turn-start-memory.ts:115` passes `prompt.slice(0, PROMPT_QUERY_CLAMP)` RAW, so for a machine-injected turn the embedded query is the `⟦turn-origin:…⟧` envelope plus loop-wake boilerplate, cut at 1000 chars — and MEASURED 2026-08-01 that is 74.4% of all turn-start recalls, with 70.0% of ALL turn-start queries truncated exactly at the clamp (251 of those 254 clamped rows machine-origin). The agent's real task content sits past char 1000 and is never embedded at all. Fix: strip the turn-origin envelope and the known wake preamble before building the query, and prefer relevance-bounded selection over a positional `slice`. NOTE the seam already exists and is already correct on the telemetry side — `describeRecallQuery` (recall-stats.ts) strips the envelope before hashing, with a doc comment explaining that not doing so would make every machine query unique by construction. The retrieval path should reuse that same stripping rather than re-implement it. Acceptance is D-033's own numbers re-run: at-clamp rate and the 15.0% exact-repeat rate should both fall materially.  — note: BUILT + LIVE-VERIFIED on :3170. stripInjectedChrome() added to turn-provenance.ts (beside parseEnvelope — one home for injected-turn format), wired into turn-start-memory.ts. 8 new tests, 48/48 green, tsc clean. LIVE A/B: an 11,860-char loop-fire wake recorded query_chars=240 on the P-048 host, against the 1000-char clamped rows every live session was recording at the same moment.

items.text: Coverage-gated degradation: when a corpus surface is below threshold, the pointer section must either sit out or mark itself degraded, instead of confidently emitting nearest-neighbours from a near-empty index. Injection needs this MORE than interactive search — a human sees a bad result list and re-queries; an agent gets one silent block and no signal.   — note: ← WI-37380 completed (done)

items.text: STOP ANDING THE LEXICAL LEG. `plainto_tsquery` ANDs every lexeme, which is why query length is currently inversely proportional to recall (measured in `corpusQueryText`'s own docstring: 5 lexemes → 0 rows, 2 lexemes → 3 rows). ⚠ **D-062 FALSIFIED THIS ITEM'S ORIGINAL PRESCRIPTION** — measured live against the real 421k-row corpus, not reasoned. A flat `|` scored by `ts_rank_cd` puts every precise match at positions **36, 41, 64, 153, 213, 277, 427** while the leg admits **6**, because `ts_rank_cd` scores term FREQUENCY and cover density and cannot express query-term COVERAGE; under AND the filter guaranteed coverage, so the ranker never had to. `websearch_to_tsquery` is not even a semantic change — it ANDs too. The real lever is **coverage-graded** ordering (distinct lexemes matched DESC, then `ts_rank_cd` DESC), which restores the 5-of-5 docs to positions 1-7 and puts a 4-of-5 doc — one AND discards outright — at 8. Preferred shape is a **CASCADE**: today's AND query first (unchanged, 73ms), relax only when it under-fills, so stage 1 is byte-identical and there is no regression by construction. Acceptance must include the leg's **2s whole-leg bound** as well as the bench: the naive per-row coverage subquery costs **745ms on ONE source**. Coupled with P-018, not strictly before it (D-062 R3).  — note: ← WI-8579 completed (done)

It currently keeps `the two longest distinct content terms`, and its own docstring concedes length is `a crude distinctiveness proxy ... used deliberately in place of a tuned constant because there is no corpus-frequency signal on this path yet`. items.text: CHEAPEST-FIRST CASCADE rather than an always-on rewriter — the design that answers D-046's latency/cost objection instead of refusing it. The Coverage Illusion (2026-05-26) measured that synthetic query distributions imply >90% of queries need LLM augmentation while REAL traffic needs 27.8%; their cascade cut latency 31.8% and avoided the LLM on 72.2% of traffic. Shape for us: statistical path always; escalate only when a query-performance predictor (clarity score — Cronen-Townsend et al. 2002) says the result distribution is unfocused. ⚠ The SAME predictor is the degradation signal P-003 needs, so build it once and use it twice.  — note: ← WI-37504 released

items.text: MAKE EDGES RETIRE THEMSELVES — treat a reaped/ended member as an implicit expiry at READ time in `listCouplingsFor` (EI-20185949236150766). Today 4 of 7 live declared edges point at agents whose presence row is already gone, and they are still returned, unioned, and rendered with `inRoster:false` on every coupling-resolving read. WHY READ-TIME RATHER THAN A REAPER: an agent that no longer exists cannot be a relevant peer by definition, so retirement then needs neither agent cooperation nor a scheduled sweep, and can leave no residue. This SUPERSEDES the 'agents never call coord:decouple' adoption problem rather than nagging agents about it — retirement stops depending on anyone remembering. ⛔ MUST NOT DELETE ROWS: D-061 R4 requires suppress-don't-delete, and the same reasoning means a retirement must not be resurrectable by the next derivation tick. Use the liveness ORACLE, never `last_active_at` — a warm-dead session reads heartbeat-fresh.  — note: ← WI-37989 completed (done)

items.text: DECIDE (do not assume) whether `coord:couple` should default a TTL. Today 6 of 7 edges carry no TTL and are therefore permanent by default, and the table comment says a TTL is for the 'couple us for the next hour while we share this file' case — which is arguably the COMMON case, not the exception. Sequenced after P-005 deliberately: if read-time liveness expiry lands, a TTL may be redundant for the dominant failure (dead-agent edges) and would then only serve the live-but-finished case. Decide with that in view and RECORD the decision either way; a default nobody chose is how the current 'permanent by default' arose.

Sequenced after P-005 deliberately: if read-time liveness expiry lands, a TTL may be redundant for the dominant failure (dead-agent edges) and would then only serve the live-but-finished case. Decide with that in view and RECORD the decision either way; a default nobody chose is how the current 'permanent by default' arose. blocked-by: P-005

items.text: MAKE THE GRADE RECURRING, so a relation going dark is seen without someone hand-querying live data. D-088 asked for exactly this and named P-006 as its home: 'a derived-signal firing count, per relation, over a window — a relation that computes 0 edges across a whole window is either dead or the flag combination gating it is unreachable, and either way a human should see it.' The dead-derived-signal detector was BUILT (parent P-007, done) and the `auto-coupling-health` rubric now grades it — but every instance of this failure class so far was caught only because a human went looking. Wire the scorecard to a cadence and route its verdict somewhere a human actually reads. NOTE: all three prior failures were green in every test at the time, so this is not test coverage — it is the standing check that distinguishes 'signal is correct' from 'signal never runs'.

items.text: Tauri shell supervises its serve.mjs child (FIXES WI-1878 — close that work-item on completion). File: `papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`. The shell already (a) spawns `serve.mjs --ensure`, (b) polls `~/.papercusp/operator.json` at boot until pid-alive + HTTP reachable — REUSE that polling code for the steady-state monitor. Add an async task (tokio) that every 30s checks: operator.json pid alive AND `GET /api/health` on the discovered port answers 2xx within 5s. After 3 consecutive failures: IF the shell owns the child (the State struct records whether --ensure spawned fresh vs reused a foreign operator — see the file-top comment ~lines 4–15 and the `Option<Child>` field around line 66; a REUSED operator must NEVER be killed/respawned by us) → kill any remnant child, respawn `serve.mjs --ensure` with the uniform backoff (1s/5s/15s/60s); ≥6 respawns/10min → stop, emit a Tauri event `operator-dead` to the webview + an OS notification. If NOT owner → no respawn, just the `operator-dead` surfacing. Implement the backoff/flap counter as a PURE state machine (struct + methods, no I/O) so it gets `#[cfg(test)]` unit tests (cargo test — follow the existing test module pattern in `apps/tui/src/main.rs` if main.rs has none). Verify (the exact WI-1878 repro): `cd papercusp-desktop && npm run dev`, `pkill -TERM -f serve.mjs`, confirm respawn within ~45s and the operator recovers (embedded PG + MCP back); then kill 7× rapidly and confirm give-up + operator-dead event instead of an infinite loop.  (← WI-3246 released) (← WI-3246 completed) (Closed via WI-3246: already-fixed/currently green. Targeted cargo tests passed: serve_respawn 6/6, operator_dead 1/1, supervision 6/6. Linked WI-1878 terminal update was rejected locally because it is remote-authored; WI-1878 thread already has packaged-app Mac VM live repro pass on build bb48d227.)

items.text: H1 [LANDED 2026-07-02] presence sessions owner_id spoofing bound to signer. ROOT: admittedDeviceSet -> admittedDeviceMap (device_pubkey->attested githubUserId); the gossip gate isMemberDevice -> resolveMemberIdentity returns the attested id. RESIDUAL: owner_id spoofing WITHIN the attacker own gh (opaque session ids, not authority-bound) — mitigated by broadcast-delivery + receipts; full closure needs owner_id<->device authority + LIVE-1.  (← WI-1475 resolved)

Sampled at 10%, those two columns extrapolate to ~960 MB of the heap while the four columns these aggregates actually read total ~82 MB — so every seq scan drags ~18x the bytes it uses. Options in preference order: (a) `ALTER TABLE ... SET STORAGE EXTERNAL` on both columns so they toast out of the heap, measure, and keep only if it wins; (b) vertical-split into a side table keyed by id. This is the "columnar insight" obtained WITHOUT an extension. Measure before AND after — do not assume.

items.text: Bootstrap DBOS against the embedded PG. Use the **functional API** (Phase 0 — DBOS bootstrap against embedded PG functional API. DONE D-013, commit 0443ccb7. Plan superseded; canonical record in the 4 shipped dbos-* plans.) (`DBOS.registerWorkflow` / `DBOS.runStep`), **not** decorators — the operator transpiles under tsx/esbuild (`:3070`) and Next/SWC (`:3055`), which handle decorators inconsistently. Call `DBOS.launch()` **exactly once**, in the non-HMR Node host (`apps/operator/instrumentation-node.ts`, where the other workers boot), with a clean shutdown on Tauri quit so HMR can't re-register/leak pollers. Resolve the connection via `getHarnessAdminUrl()` and **fail loudly if no embedded-pg discovery file exists** rather than silently hitting the dead native `:5432` (`papercusp_legacy`) fallback. Confirm system schema = `dbos`, embedded PG `max_connections` headroom (DBOS pool + ~1s/queue pollers on top of per-harness LRU pools (cap 8) + admin + scanner + SSE), and track the **DBOS system-schema migration on SDK upgrade together with the D-008 version pin** — DBOS migrates its own `dbos` schema at launch and that schema can change across SDK versions, so the two interact; resolve them as one concern, not separately. (S)

Three questions, each answered from a live isolated shell pinned to slug=papercusp, not from reading source: (a) does setting the `wif` plan filter narrow the graph at all? (b) for a plan whose items are OUTSIDE the list's 500-row updated_ts window, does it return an empty/truncated graph — i.e. is the WI-36045 defect class alive again through a different trigger? (c) how many DISTINCT plans do the 122 graph nodes span, since that decides whether an inline facet chip-group is even viable or whether it must stay a searchable picker. Record the numbers on this item; every later item's design depends on them. Drive the filter by URL param (wif codec: key:val, clauses ~, enum list comma-separated) rather than through Radix Select, which ignores synthetic Xvfb input.  — note: ← WI-36782 completed (done)

items.text: Windows VM leg packs a DISCARDED GUI installer even on a Server-only cut — ~42min wasted ISCC on every Windows Server cut. build-windows-on-vm.sh:987-1000 builds+ISCC-packs the GUI UNCONDITIONALLY (the GUI heredoc block is not gated on roles), then the Server (SERVER_BUILD_BLOCK, :797-805). So a Windows cut that only needs the Server (e.g. WI-5600: GUI already published, republishing it is forbidden) still burns ~42min LZMA-compressing a GUI installer that is thrown away. This is DISTINCT from P-006/D-004 (which rejected a gui-only *default* because it would drop the shipped LINUX Server product) — this is the inverse: honor a SERVER-only request on Windows by skipping the GUI pack. FIX: mirror the SERVER_BUILD_BLOCK var pattern — build a GUI_BUILD_BLOCK gated on "gui" ∈ PAPERCUSP_BUILD_ROLES (add `_win_build_gui` parse next to `_win_build_server` at :772-778), so `PAPERCUSP_BUILD_ROLES="server"` skips the GUI cargo+ISCC entirely. Collection (:1111-1127) is already role-agnostic and the spanning check (:1148) handles server-only. Verify with `bash -n`. WIN: ~40-45min off every Windows Server-only cut. BLOCKED until the in-flight WI-5600 build (bvz0mwsjr) stops reading build-windows-on-vm.sh (editing it mid-run is unsafe); land immediately after. Pairs with reversing WI-5559 (Windows should build gui+server by DEFAULT, matching mac D-004's own "don't drop Server" logic — that's the WI-5600 correctness fix). Discovered during WI-5600.

items.text: ISCC installer packaging is the DOMINANT Windows-cut cost (~42min/role) and it's compression-setting-bound, NOT CPU-bound — the Windows VM already has 16 cores/32GB (host: 128c/251GB) but papercusp.iss (src-tauri/windows/inno/papercusp.iss:56-58) uses `Compression=lzma2` (high level) with NO explicit `CompressionThreads`, so it LZMA-max-compresses the ~5.7GB/50k-file bundle largely serially. FIX (alpha, NO users → installer download size is a non-issue): set `Compression=lzma2/fast` (or lzma2/normal) + `CompressionThreads=auto` → expected ~42min → ~12-18min, a ~25min/cut win across ALL platforms' Inno/packaging where applicable. MEASURE before/after per D-003 (don't claim the number without it). NOTE SolidCompression=no is already set (per-file, so the pre-compressed seed isn't re-compressed — good; keep it). Do NOT edit papercusp.iss while a cut is reading it. Discovered answering owner's "why so long / can we add VM resources" (2026-07-20): the honest answer is compression settings, not more cores. Pairs with P-011 (server-only skip) → a future Windows Server cut ~90min → ~30min.

ROOT CAUSE: `work_items/set_blocker.ts` already parks the item by calling the internal `setWorkItemStateWithAliasInfo(...)` (~line 266) rather than the `work_items:set_state` TOOL; the reaction engine matches tool-invocation events, so every reaction attached to that tool is bypassed. The state change lands, the reflection never fires. items.text: Derive the `## Now` next-pointer instead of storing it. Split `## Now` into a DERIVED pointer (computed at read time from the item graph, reusing the existing importance ordering that `plans:items` already applies) and CURATED prose (`state:`), which stays hand-written. items.text: COMPACT SCHEMA PROJECTION. Add `compactInputSchema(schema)` + `compactWireBytes(tool)` to libs/generic/tooldef (generic-first: a JSON-Schema reducer is domain-free). It preserves everything a model needs to form a VALID call -- property names, types, the required set, enum members, numeric/length bounds, oneOf/anyOf discriminators, nested object/array shape, and $defs/$ref structure (D-002 depends on $ref surviving, per schema-ref-inline.ts: $defs is what keeps duplicated sub-schemas out of the byte budget) -- and strips prose: description, title, examples, default. Tests must assert (a) every required path in the full schema is present in the compact one, (b) every enum member survives, (c) no description/example strings survive, (d) measured byte reduction across the whole live catalog is reported, not asserted at a magic number. — note: ← WI-10002270 completed (done)

items.text: THE POLICY FUNCTION. `resolveToolDelivery({ agentKind, catalog, demand, floors, budgetBytes })` -> Map<toolName, full|compact|deferred>, pure and synchronous, in packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/tool-delivery-policy.ts. Algorithm, stated so it is reviewable rather than tuned: (1) every floor tool is admitted at COMPACT; (2) remaining budget is filled by descending VALUE DENSITY = callers / bytes-at-that-tier, upgrading floors to FULL and admitting non-floor tools, whichever density is higher, until the budget is exhausted; (3) ties broken by calls, then by name so the output is stable and the diff reviewable. Unit tests cover: budget exactly exhausted, a floor that cannot fit at FULL, a zero-demand floor, an unknown tool absent from the snapshot, and determinism under input reordering. — note: packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/tool-delivery-policy.ts. resolveToolDelivery returns the Map (the spec's arrow) as a thin view over explainToolDelivery (richer record) — ONE implementation. Pure/sync, no ambient state (asserted by source probe with a positive control). agentKind is never branched on: swapping only budget+floors between two kinds swaps their maps (R-2 falsifier, asserted). 14/14 green, lint:tsc clean. A test caught a real design bug mid-implementation: a ZERO-DEMAND FLOOR was being upgraded to FULL because the 'no measured demand => no density-ranked move' rule had been applied to admissions but not upgrades; fixed in the rule, not the test.

items.text: GENERATOR + DRIFT GUARD. `npm run gen:tool-delivery` emits a generated module holding the resolved per-agent delivery map plus measured byte totals; `--check` fails on drift, wired into the gate the same way gen:tool-routing:check is. The generated file carries a do-not-edit header naming the two commands that regenerate it. — note: scripts/gen-tool-delivery.ts + generated apps/operator/scripts/tool-delivery.generated.mjs (plain .mjs so the dependency-free launcher imports it with no build step) + gen:tool-delivery / gen:tool-delivery:check. items.text: Provision the local env operators at install so the env switcher (P-013/P-014) is meaningful on a packaged machine (owner directive D-006: "make :3070/:3170/:3270/:3055 exist on the local machine as part of the install process"). Today a packaged app runs ONE sidecar on a DYNAMIC port (main.rs prod path; serve.mjs --ensure singleton; embedded PG on a dynamic port) — the switcher therefore self-hides (only 1 reachable env). The 4 dev envs differ by GIT TREE (prod=release/main, staging=staging branch, dev=working tree) + Vite HMR (:3055, dev-only), all sharing ONE RLS-scoped Postgres. Making them exist locally is a real architectural feature with a genuine fork (owner to pick approach): (A) run extra operators from the ALREADY-CLONED dogfood `papercup` source checkout (host-bootstrap clones it) on different branches/worktrees + fixed ports, sharing the embedded PG via RLS (closest to dev parity; needs a node/tsx run path + a small launcher/orchestrator + branch checkouts) — heaviest; (B) bundled multi-instance: spawn N copies of the bundled serve.mjs on fixed ports against the same embedded PG, differentiated by a MODE/tree env (lighter, but envs can't differ by source unless each points at a different checkout, so "staging vs prod" content parity is limited); (C) provision only TWO meaningful local envs (prod = the bundled release sidecar on a fixed/known port; staging = an operator on the cloned `staging` checkout), drop dev/local for users — smallest viable. Plus cross-cutting: fixed-vs-dynamic port allocation (the bar can read dynamic ports from the dev-operators endpoint, so fixed isn't required), staggered boot to avoid migration contention, per-operator operator.json discovery, and resource footprint (~400MB/operator). DELIVERABLE once the approach is chosen: the install/bootstrap brings up the chosen local operators; /api/desktop/dev-operators reports them (already does, via reachability); the switcher lights up.    (← WI-952 completed) (Launcher built env-operator-launcher.ts + 21 tests + dark boot wiring + doc; live spawn verify folded into P-008/P-010 per D-009)

items.text: Author-scoped write authority for federated plan/work-item ops (D-012 durable fix). Today plan items are keyed globally `<plan_slug>/<part_key>` and merge by pure LWW (plan-parts/store.ts), and decideMemberContentOp (harness-plan-parts.ts:164) gates only on MEMBERSHIP — so ANY member can tombstone/overwrite ANY plan. Bind each federated key to its OWNING author on first write; in author-scoped mode, honor a tombstone/overwrite of a key ONLY if authored by the owning identity OR the hive owner/moderator (moderation override). Apply to plan-parts + work-items + features projections. Add a recovery/undo affordance off the append-only device-log history. Keep CURRENT behavior (member=full write) as the default for TRUSTED hives; author-scoping is required only for `open`. Tests: a cross-author delete is rejected in author-scoped mode, accepted in trusted mode; owner/mod override works; LWW within same author preserved. items.text: `work_items:burn_down` applies `limit` BEFORE computing aggregates, so the drain leader's headline metric silently depends on a pagination arg. Identical calls, only `limit` differing: at `limit:5` → `terminal.total 0`, `delta 0`, `deltaBy.fleet 0`, `closedSince.total 0`; at `limit:2000` → `1693`, `93`, `71`. Nothing marks the aggregate as truncated — `deltaByPartitions:true` and the `basis` note still render, so it reads as a complete census of an empty queue. Fix: `limit` bounds row lists only; aggregates get their own COUNT. Guard: same fixture at `limit:N` and `limit:N*100` must return equal `terminal.total`. Filed WI-37381.  — note: burn_down.ts: censusLimit pinned to WORK_ITEMS_MAX_LIMIT regardless of caller limit + truncatedByLimit flag on the aggregate. 33/33 green.

items.text: `fleet:leader-brief` attributes idleness to the member without consulting the inference pool, so its advice inverts exactly when the fleet is starved. Measured 02:31Z: brief reported `throttled:0`, `idle_with_claimable:6`, `bench_suggested:6` and per-member advice "Wake it to re-run scheduler:get_next (coord:send wake:required)", while `fleet:capacity` reported `factor 0`, `usableAccounts 1`, and tier2 `inFlight 3` against `cap 20` with `queued 28`. Its reason text also pre-commits the reader to conclude "a claim-floor problem" if the woken member still takes nothing — and the claim floors were healthy (293 claimable of 457 matched). Every diagnostic road it offered led away from the cause. Filed WI-37161 (now done).  — note: leader-brief.ts reads the pool (buildCapacityReport + readBeeProviderAvailability); advice now says DO NOT wake / DO NOT bench, re-check fleet:capacity. 147/147 green.

items.text: Rate-limit starvation REAPS fleet members rather than crashing them, and the two are indistinguishable from the leader's side. Mechanism observed live: pool at `factor 0` → member's wake fires → no inference capacity → no turn produced → the stalled-loops guard sees a loop that never turns and auto-disarms it. System emitted "2 armed engine loop(s) auto-disarmed — fires kept LANDING with no turn produced behind them (WI-6639)" during the starvation window. This very likely also explains the wake-8 "fleet collapse" (40% of members lost in one unattended hour) that was recorded as an unexplained mystery. Fix: the disarm guard should check pool state before attributing a no-turn fire to a dead loop.  — note: SHIPPED both halves per WI-37546 (NOT as originally written — D-006 stands, no fleet:capacity gate). (A) 5th veto vetoedByToolActivity: per-loop tool-call liveness with a PROGRESS term (distinctTools>=2 || okCalls>=1) + 6h ceiling. (B) reviveDisarmedLoop: a turns-stalled disarm is no longer permanent. dead-owner path untouched (7/7 correct). 72/72 tests, lint:tsc clean.</note>

items.text: The loop goal text prescribes a metric that cannot measure the mission: "measure burn-down via `work_items:claimable` vs baseline 286". Claimable count is not burn-down — the queue gains items continuously (one bug closed this run concerned a condition bridge minting ~150 junk work-items/hour), so a perfectly performing fleet can leave that number flat or rising. The real metric is terminal transitions, which I hand-rolled in SQL with a hand-maintained p2p title regex in every query.  — note: DONE 13:4xZ — the hand-rolled half is gone. work_items:burn_down (which already computes the RIGHT metric: terminal transitions with fleet attribution) now takes `fence: 'p2p-lane'`, applying the SHARED buildP2pLaneFence() FilterNode through the SAME evaluator the claim path uses (matchesClaimSpecFilter + claimSpecSubjectFromWorkItem) — so a drain fleet measures burn-down over exactly the lane it may claim from, and the per-query title regex cannot drift from the claim scope by construction. Fence runs BEFORE the census so terminal.*/counts.*/deltaBy.* all describe one population; cohortAudit stays deliberately UNfenced (a named id dropped by a fence would report as MISSING). Reports fence:{lane,candidates,counted,excluded,note}. Evidence: testing:run burn_down.test.ts + p2p-lane-fence.test.ts = 96 passed/0 failed; lint:tsc --files exit=0 clean; lint:tool-prompts 55/55 (max=1498 < 1500). items.text: `loop:checkpoint`'s `checks` array REPLACES the carried set, so re-sending a slightly reworded claim silently drops the original. Lost carried checks twice this way. The `checksDropped` warning arrives after the write, not before. Fix: upsert-by-id, or a merge mode.  — note: Both fixes the item names, shipped. (1) upsert-by-id: optional `id` on check/wall rows; `carryRowKey` = id else claim-text, TAGGED apart, driving all four identity decisions (dedup, inheritance, merge-upsert, drop-detection); round-trips through the rendered note as a `[#id]` prefix. (2) merge mode: `rowsMode:'merge'` on loop:checkpoint → mergeCarryRows({mode}), a pure upsertOntoPrior PRE-PASS so the normalizer still applies dedup/inheritance/cap exactly once; upserts hold prior position, `replace` stays default, merge+[] is a reported no-op. Also closed an adjacent silence merge would have made likely: the row cap always ate a SUPPLIED 13th row unreported (droppedChecks compares against the PRIOR set and structurally cannot see it) → new overflowChecks/overflowWalls + overflowNote. items.text: The single biggest gap: a leader read that joins the SUBSTRATE to the ROSTER. Every leader-facing tool reasons from member-local fields and is blind to the inference pool, so under starvation they all fail in the same direction at once and converge on "wake the members" — the one action that makes it worse. Wanted: one call answering "is my fleet blocked, and at which layer — pool, claim floors, spec scope, or the members themselves?" Concretely, `fleet:leader-brief` should consult `fleet:capacity` and render "5 idle because the pool is at factor 0" instead of "5 idle, wake them".   — note: ALREADY SHIPPED under WI-37161 (done) — verified in tree, not assumed. leader-brief now emits a `layer` verdict: fleet-paused | inference-pool | spec-scope | claim-floors | members.

items.text: Per-IP cooldown (the core fix): new `ipCooldownUntil` map keyed by the egress-cache-key. On a bare-burst 429 / transport failure attributable to the CURRENT egress IP, cool down THAT IP (~bare429 backoff) and rotate to the next off-cooldown IP in the SAME account's pool on retry. The existing account-level circuit (gov.pausedUntil / egressPauseUntil) fires ONLY when ALL of the account's IPs are cooled — so the 1-IP case is unchanged, and a HARD pin rides its account's IP pool instead of erroring. Load-rig + unit tests reproducing the bare-burst-on-one-IP scenario.   (← WI-1139 completed) (← WI-1139 passed)

items.text: Per-collection chunking bench (the gate for Phase 3). Generalize packages/operator-core/lib/memory/bench/turn-truncation-width-cli.ts (the D-016 instrument) so it takes a collection (table, key, text, header) and a splitter, and run it on plans, operator turns, work items, escalations and consult questions. Same method as D-016: rank-based (MRR, recall@1 of the true parent among 59 distractors), embeds through sidecarEmbedBatch with the production document/query kinds, splits in memory (no schema needed). TWO probe classes per collection: (a) a probe drawn from PAST the 2,000-char cut, which measures the gain; (b) a probe whose true answer is a SHORT, unchunked row, which measures whether best-match pooling over chunks demotes short rows (a long row gets many more chances to match). Also compare window vs markdown splitting on plans and work items. Output: one plans:add-decision per collection (register or not, which splitter, maxChunks) carrying the numbers.  — note: ← WI-10003930 completed (done)

items.text: Registry type + generic sync engine in @papercusp/search (libs/generic/search/src/chunks/, per D-010: parameterized by a SQL client, a store descriptor and an injected hash); papercusp's registry ENTRIES and tick wiring live in packages/operator-core/lib/search/chunks/. Registry entry: { surface, parent: { table, key }, textSql, headerSql?, eligibleSql?, splitter, maxChunks, store? ('shared' default) }. The engine is turn-chunk-sync's algorithm, generalized: pick parents whose sha256(text) differs from the stored parent_sha (or that have no chunks) and whose text is longer than the parent vector's 2,000-char window; split; replace that parent's chunks in one transaction, COPYING embedding/embedding_mode/embedding_profile from any old chunk with the same chunk_sha so an edit re-embeds only the changed chunks; prune chunks whose parent row is gone (batched anti-join). Report per collection { parentsSynced, chunksWritten, embeddingsReused, pruned, parentsTruncatedByMaxChunks }, so a cut-off tail is visible and never silently dropped. Runs on the existing embed-backfill tick beside runTurnChunkSyncTick (no new scheduler), with a per-collection batch budget, round-robin. Failures are per collection, fail-open but LOGGED and COUNTED (the harness-doc sync's silent catch {} is what hid EI-24580496022910673).  — note: ← WI-10003933 completed (done)

items.text: Query helper chunkAwareVectorLeg(sql, { surface, qVec, limit, mode, parentAlias, parentFilter }), shaped to serve as a SearchSource vector leg for the hybrid engine (D-009). Returns rows of (parent key columns, distance, matchedAnchor). mode 'retrieve': the parent-vector leg and the chunk leg, each joined to the parent with the caller's filter BEFORE its LIMIT, UNION ALL, then one row per parent at its smallest distance (the D-016 pooling). mode 'gist': parent vector only. Uses hnsw-iterative-scan.ts (moved into @papercusp/search per D-010) and the active embedding-space filter, taken as an injected parameter (D-011) so this does not wait on the extraction plan. First consumer: move the session-turn leg of agent-tools/search/sources.ts (~lines 1060-1130) onto it, with a parity test showing identical result ids and order on a fixed query set before and after.  — note: ← WI-10003935 completed (done)

parsedTitle: Adjacent tool-truthfulness fixes discovered during grading
Grading integrity — audit of a terminal scorecard's grading (grade-the-grader, D-004)

items.text: **Grader eligibility must be answerable BEFORE the grade, not only at the terminal write.** Expose `recordedVettingCritics[]` plus a caller-scoped eligibility verdict on `rubrics:get`, computed by the SAME predicate `scorecards:emit` enforces — one shared function, since a second copy is exactly how the two drift. EVIDENCE: I completed a full 7-criterion grade (≈10 targeted code reads, a 21/21 test run, a live two-surface reconciliation, an audit-citation spot-check) and was refused at the terminal write with `grader_is_sole_vetting_critic`. The wasted work is the small cost. The hazard is the TIMING: at the moment of refusal the grade is finished and correct and a peer is blocked waiting, so the cheapest-looking exit is to hand the ratings to an eligible agent to re-emit — which launders a disqualified grade through a compliant card and defeats the guard entirely, while feeling like helpfulness. Moving the check earlier removes that incentive at its source. ACCEPTANCE: a sole-vetting-critic caller sees `canGrade:false` with the same refusal code before doing any grading work, and a test FAILS if the precheck and the emit gate ever disagree.

items.text: **Unresolved audit findings must not vanish from the newest audit.** `plan_audits` seq 6 recorded 0 findings where seq 5 recorded 4 — two of them `disposition:'filed'` with real refs (WI-135860, EI-21619366952853296). Graders read the LATEST audit, so filed findings silently disappear from the very record the grader consults, while the audit contract's stated intent is that a filed finding carries its ref precisely so nothing is silently swallowed. The findings still exist on the seq-5 row, so nothing was destroyed — which is what makes this easy to miss. FIX: carry unresolved `filed` findings forward across `audit_seq`, or surface `openFindingsFromPriorAudits` on the read. ACCEPTANCE: a re-audit cannot produce a findings-empty latest audit while prior filed findings remain unresolved.

items.text: **Stamp WHAT IS BEING GRADED — worktree vs HEAD vs deployed, per cited path.** A grader who reads live behaviour as evidence about uncommitted code will misgrade it, and the failure is silent. LIVE THIS SESSION: `fleet:audit` returned a bare `adv_sessions-read-failed` — exactly the lossy shape the plan under grade claims to have fixed. It was the OLD DEPLOYED build; the fix existed only in the worktree (blob 380cbd12 vs HEAD 7432fd78, with ZERO occurrences of the new cause-propagating template in HEAD). Reported as a live defect, that would have been a false finding against correct work — and it would have looked well-evidenced. FIX: the acceptance-grading context stamps each cited path's commit position, REUSING `dev:pipeline_position`'s existing resolver rather than standing up a second one. ACCEPTANCE: grading context for a plan with uncommitted cited files marks them uncommitted and names the deployed sha, so a live read can never be silently attributed to worktree code.

items.text: **`completionAuthority` must not report `committed` vacuously.** With `filesChanged: []` the check ranges over ZERO declared paths and therefore always lands `committed`, regardless of repo state — the value cannot fail, so it carries no information while reading as confirmation. MEASURED the same minute: WI-135520 (empty `filesChanged`) → `committed`; EI-21615102901369580 (2 real paths) → `proposed`, and a blob check confirmed the latter genuinely absent from HEAD. A grader or leader reading `committed` as proof the work landed is trusting a tautology. FIX: emit a distinct value (`no-files-declared` / `unverifiable`) when nothing was declared. ACCEPTANCE: an evidence-only completion never reads as `committed`.

items.text: **`projection { pipe }` over a JSON body must not return silent emptiness.** An MCP JSON result is 1–5 physical lines, so the line operators are all-or-nothing: a non-matching `grep` returns an EMPTY body — indistinguishable from a filter that worked and legitimately found nothing — and a matching one returns the whole payload unreduced. This produced false ABSENCE readings during grading, which is the single most dangerous shape of wrong answer for a grader. FIX: detect a JSON body under `pipe` and emit a diagnostic pointing at `pick`. ACCEPTANCE: a non-matching grep over a JSON body returns a warning, never bare silence. — note: Moved intact to grading-adjacent-tool-truthfulness-2026-08-27#P-001 per D-001; existing EI evidence consolidated there.

items.text: Cut per-peer perf-rig process footprint so a >64-peer mesh is measurable on this box at all. D-019 next-action (i): decideMeshCapacity() (perf/host-capacity.ts) refuses 80+ peers today because each peer-child is a ~450MB OS process, so 256 peers needs ~115GB against ~70GB MemAvailable. D-020/D-021/D-022 localize the dominant term: peer-child imports @papercusp/db-org purely as an import-graph side effect (~30 chains through boot.ts) and never queries Postgres, and the barrel's eager `export * as generated from './generated'` instantiates the whole generated schema at module load. Deliverable: make the generated-schema namespace load lazily so a process that never touches `generated.*` and never opens a drizzle connection does not pay for it, then re-measure the per-peer floor and the capacity ceiling decideMeshCapacity() admits.  — note: ← WI-40385 completed as already fixed; no-PG perf-child loader, fail-loud stub, drift guard, post-loader capacity model; 27/27 focused tests and scoped lint:tsc clean at stable HEAD 603006873a.

items.text: H1 (pool): the capacity-walk returns the FIRST healthy account, not the least-loaded — THE cascade mechanism: a mass-pause flips N accounts and the in-flight wave all walks to the same first-healthy account + 429s it. Fix: collect healthy candidates in the bounded walk, pick lowest-utilization (mirror the soft-pause walk) (gateway.ts:1165-1183). Complements the shipped admission clamp.  (H1 DONE+DEPLOYED+LIVE. The capacity-walk now COLLECTS the least-loaded lowest unified-utilization healthy candidate across the bounded walk instead of early-returning the FIRST one — so a mass-pause no longer stacks the in-flight wave onto one first-healthy account the aviynw→definitelyahuman cascade. Routes to the account with the most residual budget; together with the shipped admission clamp which caps the burst size this keeps the wave off a single account. 98 routing tests green gateway + gateway-thorough; deployed clean, zero errors. REFINEMENT NOTE lower priority: lowest-util is a snapshot so it doesn't perfectly fan CONCURRENT picks they can still pick the same lowest-util account before in-flight updates; a true per-pick spread round-robin among healthy, or in-flight-aware is a possible follow-up — but the clamp already bounds the concurrent burst, so this is sufficient for the observed cascade.)

items.text: H10 (DONE+LIVE 2026-06-23): the half-open readmit required 2 STRICTLY-consecutive successful probes, and any failed probe hard-reset the streak to 0 — so on a loaded box (probes legitimately take 1.3–6.1s) or a recovered-but-jittery proxy, one slow probe perpetually restarted the streak and the account never readmitted before its pause elapsed. Fix: a failed/errored probe now DECREMENTS the streak (Math.max(0, streak−1)) instead of resetting — a mostly-healthy proxy still climbs to readmit; a dead one stays at 0. 9 egress tests green; deployed, live.

items.text: H11 (DONE+LIVE 2026-06-23): under an AIMD storm the tier-1 reserve over-reserved to ~75%. When AIMD shrank the cap to the floor (4 of 24), setMaxConcurrent re-CLAMPED the absolute reserve (4 → maxConcurrent-1 = 3), so 3 of 4 live slots were reserved for tier 1 and su + every bee tier shared ONE slot — exactly when the fleet needs throughput. Fix: store the reserve FRACTION at construction + rescale tier1Reserve = round(cap × frac) on every setMaxConcurrent (clampReserve still guarantees ≥1 shared slot). At the floor the reserve is now 1, leaving 3 of 4 for tiers >1; scales back on recovery. 20 priority-admission tests green (incl. the rescale assertion); deployed, live.

items.text: H12 (DONE+LIVE 2026-06-23): both absorb re-acquires (stall-absorb + 429/529-absorb) called gov.acquire WITHOUT a signal, so the self-heal valve / hard-ceiling abort (which only aborts the per-attempt currentAc — already settled during a re-acquire) couldn't interrupt the parked acquire. A "reclaimed" request kept waiting the full ~90s absorb budget after being declared freed → mis-reported self-heal progress + risked reclaiming a 2nd genuinely-stuck slot. Fix: a STABLE per-request AbortController (reqAbort), aborted by both the ceiling timer and the inFlightReg reclaim, passed as opts.signal to both absorb re-acquires; acquire() checks signal.aborted each loop iteration → a reclaim truly cancels it. 67 egress+gateway tests green; deployed, live.

It is installed as an extension but NOT in `shared_preload_libraries`, so it captures nothing — there is currently zero query-level visibility, which is why no slow-query data exists for any of the prior rounds. Add `pg_stat_statements` (+ `track_io_timing=on`, raise `track_activity_query_size` 1024→4096) to `shared_preload_libraries`; requires a coordinated Postgres restart on a SHARED 5-DB cluster (papercusp+bytebotdb+chatwoot+odoo+litellm) → own the `db:migrate`/named resource lock + coordinate the restart window. This UNLOCKS P-003.

items.text: P-008: Jev transport whose answer survives a busy calling thread (worker thread + synchronous drain at the deadline) — [self-imposed, evidence D-003] Since 02:06Z, 17 of 21 newer-build timeouts had ELU >= 0.9 on the calling thread; P-007 (one setImmediate deferral) rescues an answer only if it is fully buffered by the next poll phase. Design: run the Jev fetch + JSON parse in a per-process worker_thread that owns the keep-alive dispatcher (jev-transport.ts) and posts { answer, workerLatencyMs } on a MessagePort. On the main thread, when the deadline timer fires, call receiveMessageOnPort(port) synchronously before declaring timeout: an answer the worker completed within the deadline is used even though the main thread was busy. A genuinely slow Jev still times out at 800 ms (worker-measured). Record both workerLatencyMs and main-thread latency in decision_model_calls so the split stays measurable. Acceptance: a test that blocks the main thread past the deadline while a local server answers in 100 ms gets an answer; a server that answers at 1,200 ms still times out; then on staging, timeouts with ELU >= 0.9 drop to ~0 over >= 1,000 calls. Seam: libs/generic/decision-model createDecisionClient already accepts an injected fetch; the worker transport plugs in there without touching consumers.  — note: Live acceptance met: 6/1,004 (0.60%) on new builds 04:13-05:53Z; residue attributed (calling-thread ELU 0.84-1.0, post-restart + box load); worker-side timing follow-up WI-10005319. WI-10005266 done.

items.text: Normalize LIVE MEASUREMENTS out of the dedupe identity. Before computing identity for an observation or idea, strip/bucket embedded numerics — N/M tick ratios, signal counts, percentages, byte counts, timestamps, elapsed times. This is the actual root cause: `fires on 92/92 ticks` and `fires on 97/97 ticks` are one bug, but textual identity can never match them because the number is genuinely different every time. ACCEPTANCE: the 7 known insight-staleness filings and the 4 stalled-claim filings each normalize to a single identity; a regression test asserts numeric variance alone cannot mint a new identity.  — note: ← WI-36772 completed (done)

items.text: RETIRE delete-based observation retention (`runObservationRetention` in harness/improvements/hygiene.ts + its wiring in routines/improvement-actions.ts). Owner directive 2026-08-08 verbatim: 'I dont think we should have the 1k or 30 day limit. why would we ever want to throw out observations?' Note the 1000 hard cap is structurally INERT regardless — it is ANDed with the 30-day window, and at 491 observations/day ~14,730 rows are always inside that window, so the cap can never bind. The effective policy is a plain 30-day TTL that HARD-DELETES (destroying history) and whose level scales linearly with fleet activity. ACCEPTANCE: no observation is hard-deleted; if a storage bound is still wanted it is expressed over CONSUMED rows only, and as archive/rollup rather than DELETE.   — note: Delete path + deleteIssues primitive removed; recurrence guard added. See D-029 + correction D-030.

items.text: Fix the observation POPULATION SPLIT. Two different definitions of 'the observation lane' are in use and they disagree: 15,432 rows carry `lane='observation'` but only 15,154 carry the `papercusp-observation` topic tag that `listIssueAgesByTopic` joins on — and of the 688 rows older than 30 days, 357 lack the tag and are therefore invisible to every topic-joined reader, permanently. Pick ONE canonical population (the `lane` column is the better identity — it is on the row, not a join) and make readers/sweeps/panels agree. ACCEPTANCE: an anti-drift test asserts the two definitions return identical row sets. — note: ← WI-36776 completed (done)

items.text: DIAGNOSE why not one of the blender's 478 open work items has EVER been claimed or attempted (both counters are literally 0), when 404 of them sit in the claimable view and are therefore NOT gate-blocked. This is an investigation item producing WRITTEN findings, not a speculative fix — the cause is not established. Hypothesis to test first (mine, unproven): every item is framed as a design bet ('prior art -> Mechanism -> The bet') sized as a redesign rather than a bounded task with acceptance criteria, so an agent scanning the queue sees 464 open-ended design projects and takes none. Competing hypotheses worth excluding: ranking/priority places them below everything else; a claim-spec view that never covers them; or item_kind/severity making them invisible to the schedulers agents actually pull from.  — note: ← WI-36777 completed (done)

items.text: RIGHT-SIZE blender output per P-007's findings. items.text: EXPLAIN the landing-rate cliff. Blender-routed items landed at 18% in week 29 (34 of 189), then 1.4% in week 30 (3 of 216), then ~0 since. Recency partly explains the most recent weeks — items routed days ago have not had time to be worked — but it does NOT explain the week-29-to-week-30 drop, which is between adjacent weeks with near-equal elapsed time. Something changed around week 30 and the cause is NOT established. This item is to find it, not to assume it; it may turn out to be the same cause as P-007, in which case fold it in and say so. ⟵ D-034 RE-HOMES P-008 clause (2) HERE (CONTINUOUS DRAIN), not dropped: blender output is triaged on a bounded standing cadence rather than in bursts, measured as the share of terminal transitions occurring outside a >=5x-median-rate burst window, against the unchanged baseline in which 235 of 249 closures (94%) fell inside a single five-day burst (2026-08-02 to 08-06). ESTABLISHED INPUTS from D-034 (measured, not assumed): (i) NO system routine has ever closed one of these items — `improvement-triage` "records routing metadata; explicitly never dispatches" (routine-classification.ts:356), so cadence-tuning it is a FALSIFIED lever; (ii) all 234 attributable terminal transitions carry an `su-*` owner, so drain is agent behaviour, not automation; (iii) the historical drain is DISPOSAL, not consumption — 205 drops vs 40 dones (5.1:1). ⚠ The auto-close BUILD implied by continuous drain is OWNER-GATED per D-034(c): on that 5.1:1 base rate it would function as an auto-DROPPER. — note: ← WI-36781 completed (done)

items.text: Filing-time dedup enforcement in improvements:capture. CALIBRATION CONSTRAINT: my own audit filing sat at 0.85-0.86 against four genuinely-distinct items, so a naive 0.85 refusal threshold is wrong. The item's CALIBRATION CONSTRAINT was honored, not bypassed: measurement showed real duplicates (0.861-0.892) OVERLAP genuinely-distinct pairs (0.857-0.868), so pure cosine cannot separate them and the naive 0.85 refusal was correctly rejected. items.text: VM boot durability: fix OpenCore so a reboot can't re-wedge at the picker (default boot entry = Macintosh HD + picker timeout in config.plist on OpenCore.qcow2's EFI partition). Unify the launcher split-brain: the service runs `boot-sonoma.sh` (16 GB, attaches the new Tahoe BaseSystem.img installer) while the live VM came from `boot-sonoma-durable.sh` (32 GB, no installer, qmp.sock + pidfile) — point the service at the durable script and re-enable it. D-001 (root cause: ScanPolicy=0 listed OpenCore's own ESP as the DEFAULT entry → Timeout=2 auto-boot = infinite EFI self-loop the Jun 9 wedge + reproduced twice today. Fixed ScanPolicy 0→0x10303 APFS/HFS on SATA only; ESP never listed — cold boot now reaches sshd UNATTENDED. Service runs boot-sonoma-durable.sh Type=forking + QMP ExecStop)

items.text: Give memory_canonical a first-class discriminator between MEMORIES and GRAPH ENTITY NODES (D-013). Today the only difference is the presence of a jsonb key (`payload->>'entityType'` + `linkedMemoryIds`), so every naive count over the table over-reports the memory corpus by ~8× (33,478 rows vs 4,089 actual memories) — which is exactly how this plan came to believe in a 28k-row 'fragment debris class' that is really a working entity index, and nearly purged it. Options: a real `row_kind` column with an index (migration; scope entity rows out of every memory read path by default), or a separate table. Also worth deciding: whether entity nodes should be recall-eligible at all, and whether they should count toward any corpus/size metric or ship in a seed. Whatever is chosen, add a recurrence guard: a test asserting that the canonical 'how many memories do we have' read excludes entity nodes, so the 8× over-count cannot come back.  — note: ← WI-9355 completed (done)

Dormant today (no dump exists, nothing sets the var); make it refuse by default. — note: DONE 2026-08-08. Both clauses closed, and the guard now actually RUNS.
