(2) The silent carry-forward is covered: the WI-3346 republish overlay loop is asserted to stay the two-entry allowlist (source.tar.zst, env-sidecars) and to never widen to a wholesale copy of the outgoing bundle. (3) THE REAL REMAINING WORK, found today: the recurrence guard sidecar-no-database-bake-guard was committed and passing but NEVER EXECUTED — test:shell enumerates its files BY HAND and nothing named it. Measured: 16 test files on disk, 14 reachable from `npm test`; the two orphans were this P-011 guard and updater-e2e-vm (static analysis, no VM, 156ms — it had a dedicated script nothing chained). Both are now in test:shell. Fixed as a CLASS, not a one-off: a new test-registry-coverage guard fails…

items.text: Restore the NO-OUTAGE sparse cut: let the LIVE operator produce a head snapshot on demand, so a sparse seed can be cut without quiescing (D-012). Today only the writable/quiesced cut branch can append the head snapshot a sparse cut requires; the WI-4487 read-only path holds no write lock, so P-014's guard correctly REFUSES sparse there and falls back to an honest full cut — which still ships ~1.9GB. Mechanism to design: an operator-side one-shot `produceLogSnapshot` on the booted harness's own log (getBootedHarness is already exported from boot-all.ts:624), requested by the cutter and awaited before its read-only open (cut-seed-cli.ts, after waitForOperatorDrain, before the openStore readOnly at the `if (!sourceWritable)` block). ⚠ COST TO DESIGN AROUND, measured during P-013: produceLogSnapshot reads the ENTIRE own log ([0,length), log-snapshot.ts:414-419) — 461,475 blocks today — and boot.ts runs compaction INSIDE the serialized merge block, so a one-shot at this size would stall the merge loop for the duration. That cost is why the periodic cadence is 1-per-1000-ops, and it applies wherever the snapshot runs (the quiesced path pays it too). Do NOT route around this by flipping SUBSTRATE_LOG_SNAPSHOT: it is a genuine case:'incomplete' dark flag gated on the P-008 two-machine convergence proof, and it is read ONCE at boot (boot.ts:1939-1940) so it would need an operator restart anyway.  — note: ← WI-9635 completed (done)

items.text: mode:list / mode:get / mode:set defineTools. mode:list = the cheap index (each mode: name + one-line when-to-use). mode:set { mode, agent?, reason } — self OR another agent; reason MANDATORY and delivered to the target as a coord message; effect lands at the target's NEXT turn boundary (injected like a wake directive — never mid-turn); every change writes a mode_changes audit row; rate-limited so two agents cannot mode-war; OWNER-STICKY carve-out (D-003): a peer cannot override an owner-set mode — it becomes a request the owner/target sees. items.text: **`/api/desktop/git-pipeline` costs ~2s and is polled every 30s for decorative data (D-008).** MEASURED live: 2095 ms, 2107 ms, 2042 ms per call. `EnvSwitcherBar.load()` (apps/operator-vite/src/components/env-switcher/EnvSwitcherBar.tsx:140) fetches it on a `REFRESH_MS = 30_000` interval, and the component itself documents the result as decorative ("stats are decorative — never block the bar"). Two seconds of work every thirty seconds for enrichment nothing depends on. NOTE this is now an IPC call, not HTTP (D-008 fixed the transport), so it no longer holds a libsoup socket — but the ~2 s of server-side work is unchanged and still lands in the concurrency gate alongside real user reads, which is exactly what D-001 forbids. Fix: make it demand-driven (fetch on bar open/hover) or push it over the existing SSE invalidate channel rather than polling; if it must stay polled, it belongs in the background lane P-004/P-005 defines, never ahead of a user. Also observed: it fires TWICE at an identical startMs at mount — dev StrictMode double-invoke, so re-measure against a production build before claiming that duplicate is real.  — note: D-039: ~2s refuted under the item's own 30s cadence (0.18-0.22s). Real defect was hand-rolled fetch+setInterval duplicating the PRECOMPUTED dev.gitPipeline sync query; EnvSwitcherBar migrated to useSyncQuery. Route + interval deliberately kept.

items.text: Fix the 220 invalid `locks:acquire` calls. Every one carries `{"wait":{"max_sec":0},"paths":[],"intent":"tool_call:write","ttl_sec":1200}` — an empty `paths` array, which the tool rejects by contract. Identical args with no model involvement means it is harness-emitted: the OMP write-lock path never resolves the file it is claiming a lock for. Two defects to separate — the caller not passing paths, and a lock claim that can fail 220 times without anything escalating.  — note: ← WI-38080 completed (done)

items.text: Anthropic terms compliance review before public release [owner:Avi 2026-09-29, #932]. Licensing is fine: the Agent SDK (0.3.263, ships a 206 MB unmodified `claude` binary per platform) is governed by Anthropic Commercial Terms; our repo only declares it as a dependency, and the 0.0.25 macOS Server app bundles no @anthropic-ai package (0 of 19,980 entries; 8,813 node_modules entries as positive control). The RISK is auth, per code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance + agent-sdk/overview: third-party products may not offer claude.ai login or rate limits, route requests through Free/Pro/Max credentials on users' behalf, collect/store/intermediate Claude.ai credentials, or pay for/resell Claude usage for end users; users must bring their own API key or sign in to the UNMODIFIED claude binary via Anthropic's own flow. Review before shipping publicly: inference-gateway account pooling (spawn-env.ts: gateway strips + reinjects the routed account's OAuth), claude-credential-sync.ts (rewrites claudeAiOauth bundles), account linking / p2p honor-account-resolution.ts, hosted-workspace credential delivery, and the cloud subscription (cannot include Claude usage we pay for). Branding: no 'Claude Code' in names; 'Powered by Claude' is allowed. Owner option: ask Anthropic sales for approval.  — note: Rail extended with 'gateway-reinjection' (spawn-env.ts gatewaySpawnEnv) + tests 23/23 (runIds 20165688/20165689), typecheck clean; hosted-tier rule recorded for P-016 (D-014); branding compliant.

items.text: WI-5672 ROOT CAUSE — the FIRST cold restart after a fresh join fails to re-establish replication within 90s, while LATER restarts recover in ~3s. Newly characterized 2026-07-25 (su-055ae): a targeted `local-matrix.sh --only=replication_soak` run (where the soak IS the first restart) failed cycle 1 in BOTH directions and passed cycle 5 in 3s; in the full matrix the same cold-start effect lands on restart_durability(80) + reconnect_catchup(85) — which poll 270s and still miss — and is gone by soak(87). Serve-log evidence: `replication_stalled (no_replicator) ... 0 live replicator peers for 181s (was previously replicating)`. THE LOAD-BEARING EXPERIMENT, answer it BEFORE writing any fix: does replication RESUME POSITION across a reconnect, or restart COLD? Prior trace (do NOT redo): no in-tree call site overrides hyperdht connectionKeepAlive and `new Hyperswarm(opts)` does not forward it — you must pre-construct `new DHT({ connectionKeepAlive })` and pass `{ dht }`; call site cross-hive-frame.ts:67. But 5s keepalives DO fire and the socket still dies at ~13002ms, so a constant bump is a cheap DIAGNOSTIC, not the fix.  — note: ← WI-5763 completed (done)

items.text: SCENARIO-ASSERT INTEGRITY AUDIT (generalizes the WI-5715 class — high leverage). WI-5715 held this release gate red for its ENTIRE history via an assert that could never pass (unscoped in time AND harness, and blind to recovery), while everyone attributed the red to an unrelated real bug. Audit EVERY scenario in papercusp-desktop/bin/lib/scenarios/*.sh + bin/deb-hetzner-*.sh for the two failure modes: (1) CAN-NEVER-PASS asserts — a negative assert contradicted by a positive one, an unscoped grep over a cumulative log, a condition the scenario's own design guarantees to violate; (2) CAN-FALSELY-PASS asserts — a probe whose failure to RUN reads as clean (empty output treated as falsy, `grep -c` on a missing file, a swallowed ssh/exec error). The fix pattern is already landed in deb-hetzner-restart.sh: window-scope, entity-scope, correlate against recovery, and score an unmeasurable probe as FAIL. Every 'couldn't measure' must be a FAIL, never a pass.  — note: ← WI-5768 completed (done)

GIT: foreign workspaces get a FULL CLONE (own object database) on a quota volume — X4: a git worktree shares the ODB via commondir, so a quota on the checkout alone is void and a foreign `git add` of a huge blob would poison the shared, federated repo; alternative: isolated GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY; results publish by PUSH with a size/blob-cap at the results-channel admission (P-108). COMPUTE: C10 — cgroups/ulimits enforce CPU/RAM/disk/bandwidth caps mechanically (allotments are inference-myopic; a zero-token build job can eat the machine). NETWORK: C11 — per-fleet egress allowlist + logging (host's IP = host's liability; explicitly NOT origin-proxying). LOOPBACK BOUNDARY (X1 — v1-blocking for tier 2): the gateway (:8788, pooled credentials), PG (:5432), and operator API (:3070/:3170) are reachable from any foreign shell, bypassing EVERY economic control; required: per-foreign-session gateway credentials with the gateway refusing unattributed loopback calls (storm-circuit client-identification is the starting point), PG credential isolation (foreign sessions never inherit DATABASE_URL / getHarnessAdminUrl), port-filter or netns for the sandbox tier. PLUS (leader strengthening, D-015): ON-DISK CREDENTIAL isolation — a foreign session running as the host OS user can read ~/.papercusp/superuser-token, embedded-pg.json, gateway key material; the sandbox tier therefore needs a dedicated OS user or userns, not just port rules. Until the loopback boundary exists, tier 1 (P-005, same-owner) is the ONLY safe tier. X13 — enforced kill after wind-down grace. Poison-SCREENING stays post-v1 (isolation is blast-radius control, not detection). — note: ← WI-1736 dropped

items.text: Capability-grant schema: new federated table p2p_peer_grants riding the table-op path, receiver-enforced (M6/L9 pattern, never sender-asserted). Grants keyed by GitHub NUMERIC user-id — logins display-only (X9: logins are mutable + reusable; precedent: hive/member-tier-gate.ts keys github_user_id) — resolved ONLY through attested devices. Capabilities {chat, steer, work-offer, wake, spawn, read-artifacts} + presets Observer(chat) / Collaborator(+steer) / Delegate(+work-offer,wake) / Operator(+spawn). Grantee is POLYMORPHIC {fleet-slug | pool-id} (D-010). Baked amendments: C3 — thread the hive-home workspace via the shared resolver + regression test asserting write/capture/drain agree (WI-1564 class). C6 — grant/revocation enforcement reads BYPASS cache tiers (read-through; WI-1547 class). M9 — wake is a token-burning DoS: rate-cap wakes per grantor, metered separately. m14 — optional per-device grant exclusions. M19 — grants federate USER-level (revocation lands everywhere); allotments stay PER-MACHINE. m25 — device key rotation re-anchors its attestation; grants keyed through it survive rotation (rotation must never look like revocation). X6 — grants + publisher-sets carry grantor EPOCHS; receivers track a high-water epoch per grantor; spawn-class ops refuse any record whose epoch trails high-water. Wall-clock (sender OR arrival) never gates revocation. (Lane A grants core claimed by su-71623 — P-001 then P-004) (su-71623: mig 463 p2p_peer_grants + p2p_grantor_epochs, stamp+capture triggers APPLIED+recorded; full federation wiring registry, mapper, receiver-enforced projection, register-all; lib/p2p store C3 resolver refuses default-partition, C6 direct reads, X6 epoch bump+re-stamp, M9 cap col, m14 exclusions, presets per spec; 121 targeted tests + full operator-core suite green 25748 passed)

items.text: Loud-refusal receipts: every refused cross-peer action produces (a) a receipt to the requester naming the exact missing capability/budget, (b) a local audit row, (c) a counter metric. No silent drops. Baked: M15 — unauthenticated failure paths get COUNTERS, authenticated ones get receipts (loud is not unbounded). M21 — the offer-id threads through every receipt/audit/log line on BOTH sides + a p2p:trace tool assembles the cross-machine timeline from federated audit rows. X8 — receipt taxonomy includes an EXCUSED-BREACH kind (preemption-class interruptions; excluded from reliability signals, see P-203). (Lane A continues su-71623: loud-refusal receipts + p2p:trace skeleton, M21 offer-id threading — grant-store already returns structured refusals {code, missing, detail} as the receipt payload seed) (su-71623: mig 468 receipts+counters applied; emitP2pReceipt receipt+audit+counter, M21 offer-id threaded, M15 counters wired into grant-apply refusals, X8 excused-breach kind, receiver-enforced p2p-receipts projection, p2p:trace tool live WI-1698; tsc + tests green)

items.text: Standing puller: opt-in = a supervisor-owned standing claim-spec (P-016 machinery) filtered to opted-in fleets; respects P-002 windows + caps. Baked: C1->C4 — the PUBLISHER stamps the assignment on the offer at publish time over an epoch-versioned opt-in roster; receivers VERIFY the stamp; soft designation stealable after T2 (slow-but-alive designee cannot stall work). X12 — steals are reliability-WEIGHTED and publisher-EXCLUDABLE (defeats the claim-stall-expire-resteal starvation loop). items.text: (NEW — X2) Canonical-merge admission check: commits reachable ONLY via foreign-marked refs must have author identity resolving within the offer's attested ORIGIN chain, else the merge into canonical staging is REFUSED loudly. Git author is free text and a foreign session has shell+git — without this check, a hand-crafted --author=<owner> commit federates via P-108, merges into canonical staging, and the github-bridge egresses it to GitHub permanently attributed to a human who never wrote it. Structural dual of the landed github-ingress-admission (pattern to borrow). LIVE-2 leg proves it. Call-site invariant documented in DESIGN-p2p-P109 s4.)

items.text: Inference leases: short-lived reservations for burst planning — remote {X tokens for fleet F, T min} and local {slots + optional model-residency pin}. Auto-expiring; claim-time revalidation stays authoritative (leases advise, never replace the gate). Baked: H8 — freshness measured against the RECEIVER'S OWN arrival timestamp (never sender stamps); machines advertise clock offset in presence; excess skew flagged. X6 — arrival-time freshness is ADVISORY only; revocation/dangerous paths gate on epochs (P-001). H6+X8 — lease-breach receipts feed the host reliability signal EXCEPT preemption-class interruptions, which are EXCUSED breaches (distinct receipt kind) surfaced as an expected-availability signal that scheduling prices in — a host must never be penalized for using its own machine (D-008's core promise). (su-d1985 p2p-hive-git member: inference leases as a PURE module — grant/expiry/claim-time-revalidation authoritative/H8 receiver-clock freshness/X6 advisory/X8 excused-breach receipts. Composes offer-budget.ts; no store, no /res GUI leader's P-201/P-206.) (su-d1985: inference-lease.ts pure module green 32 tests. grant/expiryH8 receiver-clock/epoch-fenceX6/clock-skewadvisory/revalidateAtClaimauthoritative — leases advise never replace/X8 breach classification. Composes offer-budget axis types; no store/GUI. Live wiring = P-202 gate consumer.) (← WI-1742 completed)

items.text: Billing matrix (D-009 — NO relay/proxy in v1) with the X7 PER-MODE AUTHORITY TABLE: (a) host-pays + allotments = default — host-SIGNED usage receipts authoritative (host spent its own money; M8). (b) pool-with-attribution — receipts + PROVIDER-BILLING RECONCILIATION, restricted to single-owner pools (M17): the credential reason AND the distinct metering-trust reason (the spender self-reports — receipts-authoritative alone would crown the self-interested party); both recorded so relaxing M17 forces revisiting the authority model. (c) provider-scoped capped keys — the provider's billing is the independent meter. The federated gateway leg is a QUOTA LEDGER, not a streaming relay. (su-c2428: billing matrix D-009, X7 per-mode authority table as a PURE policy module — which meter is AUTHORITATIVE per mode: a host-pays+allotments→host-SIGNED receipts M8; b pool-with-attribution→receipts + provider-billing reconciliation, single-owner pools only M17; c provider-scoped capped keys→provider billing is the meter. NO relay/proxy in v1 federated gateway leg = quota ledger, not a stream. New file, no scope-*.ts.) (DONE su-c2428. NEW pure module lib/p2p/billing-matrix.ts: X7 per-mode authority table — host-pays→host-signed-receiptsM8, receipts alone authoritative; pool-with-attribution→receipts+provider-reconciliation, requiresSingleOwnerPoolM17, both credential+metering-trust reasons recorded; provider-capped-key→provider-billing. resolveBillingAuthority enforces M17 + D-009 no-relay v1 gateway leg = quota-ledger only, refuses streaming-relay for any mode. isReceiptAloneAuthoritative / authoritativeMeterFor helpers. Tests 12/12 green 3 property + 9 unit; 0 tsc errors. Consumers: P-205 metering which meter to settle from, P-304 pool ledgers. No scope-*.ts, no store — pure policy.) (← WI-1743 passed)

items.text: Stop full-copy dependency-generation materialization. `cp -a --reflink=auto` copies node_modules (~17 GB) from ext4 / (nvme1n1p2) to XFS /mnt/data (nvme0n1); reflink is impossible across filesystems, so every generation is a full copy. Measured 2026-10-01 ~15:40Z: papercusp-bg-host at ~245 MB/s read and ~148 MB/s write (per-cgroup io.stat), almost all from that cp, while IO PSI full avg60 was 31–45%. Nine generations were created between 06:39 and 11:39 local. Make materialization reflink- or hardlink-cheap: put source and target on one reflink-capable filesystem, or hardlink immutable package dirs. Find why the generation key changed 9× in 5 h. Reuse the existing dependency-generation script and observations EI-24777249698580002 / EI-24781762245796803. Acceptance: matched IO bytes per generation and generations/day before vs after. Existing dependency-generation, lease and gate tests stay green; generation correctness and lease semantics are unchanged.  — note: ← WI-10004927 blocked (1 external blocker)

items.text: Async identity hooks and operation providers use catalogued events, watch:create, execution-plan P-016 bindings and existing DBOS receipts, targeting blueprint operations; never inject into the current turn. This item explicitly implements the wearer reaction principal in events/dispatch-reaction.ts; P-016 supplies binding/receipt plumbing, not that authority. Immediately before dispatch inside the durable execution boundary, resolve the attachment's live wearer; intersect wearer grants, identity-declared needs, pot/role ceiling and the class verb capability; enforce role and quota with no bypass and charge the wearer. Revalidate on replay, not from queued or previously recorded grants. Missing/changed attachment, identity version, principal, grant, binding or empty capability produces a recorded terminal refusal with zero dispatch; never fall through to system:event-reaction or plugin:event-reaction authority. Auth lookup failure also dispatches nothing and follows bounded operational recovery, never grants access. Receipt/dedupe identity includes event, wearer, rule and attachment revision; two wearers receive separate authorized effects, a replay does not duplicate one wearer's effect. Tests in the real DBOS integration suite: enqueue→detach/revoke/upgrade, missing capability at install and fire, quota/role refusal, two wearers, and SIGKILL after authorization before dispatch followed by fresh authorization on recovery. Verify invocation attribution. Cross-plan prerequisite: blueprint-backed-work-item-execution-2026-09-23 P-016 and its actual predecessors, not its P-019/P-024.   — note: ← WI-10003321 completed (done)

items.text: Make a novel third-party class contract portable through the existing signed Cupboard package/review and capability-class registry surfaces. Extend the identity's existing signed Cupboard package release with a typed class-contract payload section in its immutable content closure (not a new blueprint layer field and not by-value copies of bundled listings). Pin canonical contract bytes/schema and publisher-namespace/class@version/content hash; import through the existing classes registry. No new class/identity listing kind or parallel registry. The current classes:define tool is platform-only, so published metadata must enter the destination through a validated review/consent-controlled importer, not grant the author operator access. Pin contract, provider, inspect recipe and proof inputs; reject same-version changed bytes, publisher-namespace squatting, platform-name shadowing or schema widening, unapproved/unresolved refs and signature/contract/schema mismatches. Rerun destination conformance from actual installed registry/recipe inputs before binding; source run ids are provenance, never portable success flags. Structural success must not masquerade as behavioral proof. Verify the five Safety rules and D-009 for recipe bindings. This introduces a consent-controlled authority-registry write path: test namespace squat, platform shadow/schema widening, forged hash and rejected consent alongside the happy path. It is required implementation work, not an assertion that contract transport already exists.   — note: ← WI-10003322 completed (done)

items.text: Implement read-only recipe providers under the five Safety rules; consent-gated binding records orchestrate:inspect pins, runtime reuses classifyDurableCall, and every output is schema/size validated and provenance-fenced. Implement cancellation end to end from sink deadline through orchestrate → run-script handleCall → facade.call → dispatch ctx.signal; stopping the worker alone is insufficient. Stop queued/nested dispatch at the deadline; discard late/superseded-generation results from injection and caches. A provider that ignores abort remains accounted for under a host in-flight cap, is reported, and cannot create unbounded orphan work. Tests cover egress, unknown effect, dynamic/nested target, stale pin, schema/size failure, visible timeout, no post-deadline dispatch, absent stale result on the next turn, multiple slow providers under an aggregate deadline and bounded concurrency, and detach while a call is in flight. Both direct tool and recipe bindings obey the same budget/fence boundary. Changes to libs/generic/tooldef cancellation belong here, not to the execution plan.  — note: ← WI-10003323 completed (done)

items.text: Extend cupboard:install-blueprint and attested blueprint:publish trust/consent paths, preserving pinned full-content closure and existing rollback history. Content-only installs may be free only with package-private applicability; extra grants, proposed bindings, operations, rules/events and plugin code require consent. Extend the existing lifecycle with recoverable install/update/uninstall/rollback steps and per-resource compensation using P-006 receipts (memories, docs, provider bindings, rules/subscriptions, activation last); reuse existing DBOS primitives if a durable wrapper is needed, not a new executor and not execution-plan P-019. A half-install is never applied; on failure the previous applied revision remains usable and cleanup residue is reported until repaired. items.text: Decide and execute P-004's disposition in light of D-052 and D-053. The keep-alive retention feature is SHIPPED and is a measured REGRESSION against this plan's own goal: warmSteady script cost rises monotonically with the retention limit (2080 -> 2520 -> 3270ms summed over 34 tabs for limits 1/2/3), with no measured time-to-content benefit, reproduced across two independently-ordered sweeps at load regimes differing 2.5x (+58% and +57% on the endpoint pair). The decision is NOT foreclosed by that. P-004 may still be worth keeping for reasons this plan never measured — preserved scroll position, in-progress form state, and avoided refetch on revisit are user-visible properties that a per-switch script-time metric cannot see, and `?keepAlive=0` collapsing to limit 1 means the lever already exists to tune rather than revert. What is NOT defensible is leaving it shipped at limit 3 while the only evidence anyone has says limit 3 is the worst of the three doses. Do, in order: 1. LOCALISE the cost before choosing. Both sweeps read one metric family (CDP ScriptDuration deltas), so the retained-tree mechanism is dose-consistent but still [inferred]; a trace-level pass (scripts/trace-probe.mts + trace-buckets.mts) should say WHERE the extra script time lands. If it is hidden surfaces re-rendering or keeping subscriptions live, that is also a fixable bug in RetainedSurfaces rather than an argument against retention as such — freeze harder and the cost may go away while the benefit stays. 2. Weigh the unmeasured benefits explicitly, naming them, rather than deciding on the one number this plan happens to have. 3. Choose: revert, lower the default limit (limit 2 is measurably cheaper than 3 and still retains one surface), make retention conditional on tab weight, or fix the per-switch cost and keep limit 3. 4. Record the call as a plan decision citing D-052/D-053, and re-measure the chosen configuration with scripts/perf-dose-response.sh so the plan ships against evidence rather than intent. Re-measurement needs a P-004-carrying build served somewhere isolated — D-050 has the recipe (PORTAL_BUILD_ONLY=1, isolated PORTAL_HOME); the :3082 rig used for D-052/D-053 has a hard deadline of 02:22Z on 2026-09-08 and will need rebuilding after that.  — note: ← WI-10000650 completed (done)

[inferred, to measure first] PUI runs on the alternate screen with no mouse capture (apps/tui/src/main.rs EnterAlternateScreen, no EnableMouseCapture), so most terminals turn the wheel into Up/Down keys, which while composing cycle your message history instead of scrolling the chat, and the terminal's own scrollback holds nothing. Probe: wheel-scroll in GNOME Terminal/VTE and Konsole over a long chat and record what moves. Fix so the wheel and the terminal scrollbar scroll the conversation, and text selection still works. items.text: Slash menu and keys at parity. / opens a filtered menu with one-line descriptions: /model, /help, /clear (new conversation), /resume, /status (engine, model, account, context left, cost), /compact where supported, /approvals (permission mode), /exit. ? opens a shortcuts overlay. items.text: #3 Close the release-fixer "0 real fires" loop — AND harden it against the liveness bug. The 2026-06-21 stall: the gate-fix bee DIED and was treated as active for ~1h, gate red+unowned. Whether that bee was the release-fixer or an ad-hoc Queen dispatch, the fixer is subject to the SAME dead-holder problem. Verify the release-fixer actually fires on a real red AND self-heals when its fixer bee dies (re-dispatch on dead/stalled holder). Depends on agent-activity-liveness-truth-2026-06-21 (P-003 reconciler / EI-2311).  (BLOCKED on agent-activity-liveness-truth-2026-06-21 ready but UNBUILT + UNASSIGNED — the reconciler P-014 is explicitly scoped to ride. Fire-path half is test-verified P-007: green-checkpoint:red → release-fixer spawn, 11/11. Self-heal half: the release-fixer dedup at release-actions.ts:417 is purely TIME-based signature + at<2h — never checks the dispatched fixer's liveness, so a dead fixer leaves the gate red+uncovered up to 2h the incident class. HARDENING HOOK once the reconciler lands: make that dedup liveness-aware — when it would skip, query the reconciler for the dispatched fixer's liveness/progress + re-dispatch if dead/stalled. Building a bespoke release-fixer-only liveness check now = parallel-surface anti-pattern + risky in this fleet-critical file. See D-009.) items.text: #5 STRUCTURAL: the gate is whole-tree all-or-nothing, so ONE unrelated red holds EVERY clean change hostage (2026-06-21: 2 unrelated reds blocked the ledger deploy for hours). This plan mitigates (loud + auto-fix + de-flake) but doesn't eliminate it. Investigate per-package / per-change gating, OR "deploy last-green + cherry-pick the clean change," so an unrelated red can't hostage unrelated work. The deepest fix; scope carefully.  (Design done D-010. The gate is batch-affected not whole-tree: one red in any affected workspace blocks the whole batch's FF. Recommended structural fix: longest-green-PREFIX FF promote the longest green prefix instead of nothing; preserves FF-only + single-ref deploy. Alt/surgical: cherry-pick-the-clean-change onto last-green. Owner picks A / A+D before I build — deepest live-gate change, build attended not blind.) Record search scope/coverage and unknown separately from disproven/duplicate. items.text: [Unified, D-005: also covers P-011 — re-measure only the bindings whose measured TEST or SOURCE paths moved, and run copy-out mutation probes in parallel.] SOURCE-path drift from PEER commits, not just the bound test file. P-011 re-measures when a bound TEST file fingerprint moves; the dominant staleness on turn-start-memory-two-class-2026-09-21 came from SOURCE paths rewritten by a DIFFERENT agent. Measured 2026-09-23 by su-c03852cb: R-11 proofs taken 2026-09-22T19:26Z against three measured files, all rewritten afterwards by another agent refactor (su.md 00:17Z, papercusp-files.ts 02:31Z, the guard test 03:13Z), so the proof was stale before it could be used. P-001 does not fix this: it stabilises clause identity across amendments, not evidence across unrelated commits. Fix: pin a proof to the commit it was measured at, so a proof taken against commit X stays valid for X; only the clause moving or the plan advancing its commit makes it stale. Must resolve submodule gitlinks (every migration lives in libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql). Source: decisions D-119 and D-124 on turn-start-memory-two-class-2026-09-21. — note: ← WI-10002643 completed (done)

items.text: Any-drags adequacy: supersede-on-bind, and name the dragging binding. The per-clause adequacy check evaluates EVERY live binding at the current revision, so one under-attested row fails a dimension no matter how good the evidence beside it is. Measured 2026-09-23 by su-c03852cb on R-11: after binding a fresh, fully-flagged, targeted mutation proof the bar still failed until 13 older rows were retracted by hand - so good new evidence cannot rescue a clause, and part of the fleet-wide 59% retraction figure is BOOKKEEPING rather than re-proof. Fix: plans:bind-spec-evidence supersedeAtRevision:true, atomically retracting the other live rows at that clause revision; and extend P-007 so its per-clause verdict names which binding ids drag each failing dimension. Also make the ledger requirement discoverable: execution-integrity, falsifiability and traceability are unsatisfiable without a real testRunId, and mutation-probe rows carry source=mutation-probe, which testing:runs did not surface in a filePath query. Source: decision D-123 on turn-start-memory-two-class-2026-09-21. — note: ← WI-10002644 completed (done)

Peers holding those bindings get one coord notice per edit burst, not one per edit. On this plan, peer edits staled P-001 once, P-002 twice and P-004 four times (D-006; EI-24053039097767980). Guard (Vitest): editing a bound source path yields the advisory naming that spec; an unbound path yields none.  — note: ← WI-10002735 completed (done)

Each emitted adequacy card records the evaluator revision that graded it; when that rule changes, cards graded under an older revision are re-evaluated mechanically from their stored runs, and only a changed verdict needs a new audit. items.text: Drive P-008's schema-friction pass by MEASURED per-tool failure rate — and start with rubrics:propose, which is the worst and is currently unnamed. Measured 7d workspace-wide: rubrics:propose 46/62 failed = 74.2%; rubrics:amend 250/773 = 32.3% (independently reproduces su-1bb6850b's ~32% figure from a separate session and query); plans:audit 61/386 = 15.8%; scorecards:emit 110/863 = 12.7%; plans:set-plan-status 14/294 = 4.8%. A 74% first-call failure rate on the verb that CREATES a rubric is the most expensive possible location for schema friction, because it sits at the head of every plan's acceptance path and every retry re-pays a full model turn. Corroborating instance from this session: filing a single coord:escalate card cost THREE invalid_input round trips (severity enum, title->summary, plan->plan_slug, options[] wanting objects not strings) — each refusal printed a perfect corrected call, so the information was always present; the cost is purely the round trip. Re-check: SELECT tool_name, count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE status<>'ok') FROM harness_shared.tool_invocations WHERE workspace_id='papercusp-workspace' AND invoked_at > now() - interval '7 days' AND tool_name LIKE ANY (ARRAY['rubrics:%','scorecards:%','plans:%']) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC. — note: merged into P-008 per D-005 (consolidation after five authors); P-008 now carries this scope.

Measured 2026-09-23 by su-c03852cb: 105 of 260 coord:send calls (40%) returned ok:false, dominated by the 600-char delivered-body cap - the row still persists, so the sender cannot tell what landed and re-sends by hand, and this sits on the critical path of every amendment counter-signature round trip. Fix: chunk or server-summarise and report exactly what was delivered. items.text: Refusals must name EVERY invalid field in one response, not one per round-trip. Distinct from P-008/P-017 (per-tool examples and near-miss acceptance): this is the validator contract across all tools. Observed 2026-09-23 by su-77b3a99d: coord:send refused three calls in a row for three different fields (`to` must be an array -> `expects` required -> `forYouBecause` required), each refusal naming only the first failure. Measured workspace-wide, last 24h, excluding activity:report: 1,780 invalid_input refusals, of which 541 (30%) followed another invalid_input on the SAME tool by the SAME session within 3 minutes. That 30% is an UPPER bound on this item's payoff — some chains are a second, different mistake rather than a field the first refusal hid. Fix: validate the whole argument object and return every issue together, plus the corrected call when it is unambiguous. Test: a call with three independent invalid fields is refused once, naming all three. Re-check: LAG(error_code) over harness_shared.tool_invocations partitioned by (coord_owner_id, tool_name), invalid_input after invalid_input within 3 min.  — note: merged into P-008 per D-005 (consolidation after five authors); P-008 now carries this scope.

items.text: Ship refusal names the blocking PHASE and its codes per BAR (R-9). When grading is missing or stale and pre-grading fails, plan-acceptance-gate.ts returns the ship-phase refusal with every code and discards the pre-grading verdict it just computed, so the agent must probe again to learn which one code blocks. Carry `phase:'pre-grading'`, the pre-grading codes, and a per-BAR table { barKey, contract: manual|automated, codes, nextAction } on the refusal, and lead its message with the single next repair. Measured 2026-09-23 (Avi #302): su-9306f9c3 on consult-expert-routing-2026-09-22 got six codes (evidence_plane_unmet, proof_stale, proof_depth_missing, vetting_missing, grading_missing, author_verdict_missing), re-derived by hand that only bar_snapshot_vetting_missing blocked, and mangled the per-bar codes with a regex. Guard (Vitest): a fixture with grading missing and vetting missing yields phase pre-grading, bar_snapshot_vetting_missing as the next repair, and one per-BAR row per blocked BAR.  — note: ← WI-10002733 completed (done)

Guard (Vitest): a fixture with grading missing and vetting missing yields phase pre-grading, bar_snapshot_vetting_missing as the next repair, and one per-BAR row per blocked BAR. importance: high — note: ← WI-10002733 completed (done)

items.text: Status-reporter VOLUME, not just the glance_stale bug — extends P-012, which fixes the key and gates coord:glance only. items.text: Tool-call failures auto-file tracker rows faster than anyone triages them. Measured 2026-09-23 by su-77b3a99d: harness_shared.engineer_issues rows titled '%tool-call failure%' — 5,978 since 2026-07-13, 1,707 in the last 7 days, 522 in the last 24h; by state 4,021 open, 979 done, 652 resolved, 312 dropped. Fix: file one row per (tool, error_code) signature with an occurrence counter instead of one per failure; do not file when the refusal itself returned a corrected call; fold the existing open rows into their signature rows. items.text: [Unified, D-005: "a wake with nothing to act on costs no turn", also covering P-034 and P-026 — no loop fire while parked on an await; non-actionable inbox events go to the inbox without a turn (directed asks and owner directives always wake); build wake text to budget instead of building then truncating.] Loops keep firing while the session is parked on an owner await. Distinct from P-013 (dead sessions): here the session is alive and correctly waiting, and the armed await already guarantees the wake. Observed 2026-09-23 on su-77b3a99d: loop armed 01:47Z at a 900s interval, 8 fires by 04:22Z, every one while the only lane was parked on conv-mudfz4io (a question to the owner). Each fire paid a full model turn at ~89% context and produced nothing but checkpoint rewrites. Fix: when every open lane is blocked on an armed await for an owner answer, suspend or stretch the loop until the await resolves, keeping a slow liveness heartbeat. Test: a session whose only lane awaits an owner answer takes no loop turns until the answer or the heartbeat. Measurement gap: this is ONE session's count; the fleet-wide rate still needs a query joining loop fires to pending owner-answer awaits.  — note: ← WI-10002651 completed (done)

items.text: loop:checkpoint cannot change one carried check without re-sending all of them. Measured 2026-09-23 by su-77b3a99d, workspace-wide, 7 days: 1,675 checkpoint_merge_would_evict_rows refusals across 51 sessions, plus 38 checkpoint_replace_would_drop_rows across 26. su-77b3a99d alone: 30 refusals against 77 successful writes; the recovery each time was re-sending all 12 rows (~15 KB) to change one. [inferred, unverified] An edited claim appears to be keyed as a NEW row, so at the cap an edit reads as a net addition. Fix: a per-row upsert/retire keyed by a stable row id, so changing one check is a one-row write and the cap refuses only a real net addition. Test: at the row cap, editing one existing row succeeds and leaves the other rows byte-identical. items.text: Wake text is built in full, then truncated. packages/operator-core/lib/events/await/wake-executor.ts:1724 appends `[injection-door: wake text exceeded the ~N-token per-hop injection budget and was truncated; ...]` and points the agent at a spill file, so such a wake pays to assemble text, cuts it, and then costs another read to recover it. Observed on su-77b3a99d's loop wakes 2026-09-23: the checkpoint middle is elided and `## Next action` survives only because head and tail are kept. Fix: build wake text to the budget from the start — priority-ordered sections that stop at the budget, with a named pointer for each section that did not fit — instead of cutting a finished document. Sister rule: owner-directive-delivery-redesign-2026-09-22 P-004 already forbids truncating owner directives; this extends it to the rest of the wake. Why it compounds: su-77b3a99d compacted 39 times in 30.3h (one every ~47 min), so wake size is paid many times per session. Test: no wake carries the injection-door truncation marker, and every omitted section is named with a pointer. Measurement gap: marker frequency is not in tool_invocations; a counter is part of this item. — note: merged into P-024 per D-005 (consolidation after five authors); P-024 now carries this scope.

items.text: [Unified, D-005: also covers P-015 — a consult with exchanges_used=0 at 50% TTL becomes a pullable review work item instead of cascading to the next responder.] Review recruitment is STARVED — make vetting/grading PULL, not PUSH. Measured 2026-09-23 by su-ae3c4989, workspace-wide over 7 days: 309 consults expired and 304 of them had exchanges_used=0 — the responder never took a single turn. Live-peer answer rate ~1%; mean ~29h open per expired consult. Systemic, not per-agent: su-3d6cba40 15 consults/0 answered, su-52501ad8 15/0, and even system:acceptance-grading-sweep 15/1. P-004 (vet before proof) lowers the COST of a critique but not its ARRIVAL RATE, so it cannot help when no critique ever arrives. FIX: promote the existing vettingWorkItem + critique-posts channel (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/scorecards/emit.ts, which already requires >=1 comment authored by neither the emitter nor the rubric author) from escape hatch to a first-class claimable backlog item, so review is PULLED by agents already polling work_items:claimable rather than pushed at sessions that never read their inbox. The independence predicate is unchanged, so no rigor is lost. TEST: a rubric whose vetting is unsatisfied appears in work_items:claimable for a non-implementer, and scorecards:emit accepts that work-item as the vetting channel. Re-check: SELECT state, count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE exchanges_used=0) FROM harness_shared.consult_state WHERE workspace_id='papercusp-workspace' AND created_at > now() - interval '7 days' GROUP BY 1. — note: ← WI-10002654 completed (done)

When a plan is superseded or consolidated (plans:set-plan-status superseded, or a consolidation Decision), park every non-terminal item in another plan whose deliverable is shipping or accepting that plan (a "Ship <slug>" carrier). items.text: OWNER DECISION — flip the memory-side DEFAULT embedder gemma→harrier? Data (P-006, gold set): harrier@1024 wins clearly (R@1 .8833 vs .8083, MRR .9286 vs .8677) at ~4× embed latency (258ms vs 63ms/query CPU) and ~2.4GB extra RSS if both models stay warm (prose surfaces MUST stay gemma — harrier@384 rejection-margin collapse .0705). A flip = split-brain sidecar (two warm models), full memory re-embed (UI button + reembed route are live), and default churn the same day the gemma default landed. Harrier is already user-selectable (P-014). Recommendation from the data: keep gemma default, revisit if memory-recall quality complaints surface or an fp16/quantized harrier closes the latency gap.

items.text: Machine-local lock waiter queue: wait / wake_on_grant stays per-machine, so cross-machine waiters don't see each other's grants. Route waiters through the per-Hive authority, OR document it as intentional eventual behavior (git-merge is the correctness backstop). — note: Resolved via the SECOND branch this item offers — ratified as intentional eventual behavior, recorded as Decision D-011 (WI-6047). NO behavior change. Three legs, each verified in code: (1) CORRECTNESS unaffected — acquire+release DO route to the elected authority, so grants are authority-serialized cross-machine and a machine-local waiter queue cannot double-grant; only the WAKE is local. (2) LIVENESS BOUNDED — a waiter ticket stays grant-eligible for WAKE_QUEUE_WINDOW_SEC (1800s) and a grant to an agent that never wakes is bounded by the lock TTL lease (D-004 #3). (3) FAILS LOUD — lock-grant-bridge.ts fires granted:false "queue wait ended WITHOUT a grant ... re-queue or pivot" when the wait lapses, so a cross-machine waiter is never left hanging on a grant it cannot see. Net cost is LATENCY only, with git-merge as the backstop this item names. Also upgraded file-lock-authority-wiring.ts:27 from a deferral ("a further step") to the ratified decision. Revisit only if a real workload s…

items.text: Lightweight always-on 'hive X has activity' wake signal so an idle/evicted member is activated WITHOUT holding its engine live. Depends on the Phase 3 relay tier.  — note: CARRIES P-010'S FINAL FLIP, BUT IS ITSELF DEPENDENCY-SPLIT — read before picking up. (1) P-010's mechanism is built+tested (WI-6067); it defers only NON-federating harnesses because BootAllOpts.deferFederatingHarnesses defaults false; flipping it true needs a remote wake trigger and a policy test already pins the flip. (2) THIS ITEM'S OWN TEXT says "Depends on the Phase 3 relay tier", and P-013 says the relay nodes "deliver the idle-member wake signal" — so the full store-and-forward case (wake a member that was OFFLINE when the write happened) is genuinely blocked on P-013. (3) CORRECTION to my previous note: the global hive DIRECTORY topic is NOT a safe substitute — it only reaches members that are concurrently online (no store-and-forward), and private/unpublished hives deliberately stay dark on the directory, so broadcasting "hive X has activity" there would leak private-hive metadata to non-members. (4) THE UNBLOCKED SUB-SLICE, discovered 2026-07-26: substrate-eviction-policy.ts'…

items.text: SHARDED / HIERARCHICAL lock+claim  single per-hive argmin authority (lock-authority.ts; work-item-claim-authority-swarm.ts:37) is both the throughput ceiling (all acquires funnel to one node, each an unpruned O(M) presence scan) and a fail-open SPOF (double-grants under contention). Partition the lock keyspace across multiple arbiters (e.g. by path/domain hash) so no single node serializes the whole hive; keep deterministic election per shard.

items.text: RELAY/SUPERNODE replication topology so >256 simultaneously-active peers can participate in ONE hive WITHOUT the flat O(M²) full mesh (today's 256-peer process-global cap means the mesh literally cannot form past ~256). Peers replicate via a tier of supernodes/relays (reuse always-on cloud Swarms) instead of all-to-all; content stays E2E (epoch keys) so relays are content-blind. This is the change that lifts the hard ~256 ceiling to thousands.

items.text: **A registry-read FAULT must not render as "not registered" (EI-19286551248996972).** Observed live 2026-08-01: `plans:list` returned ok:true with `plans:[]` and `plans:get` returned not_found for `papercusp`, while psql held 960 plans. Four defensible layers compose the wrong answer: (1) `harness-core.ts:371-374` + `:377-383` wrap both registry reads in bare `catch {}` that deliberately fold "unreadable" into "absent", returning a `null` byte-identical to a genuine miss; (2) `plans/source.ts:368` propagates it; (3) `plans/source.ts:412-419` restates that null as an ASSERTION ABOUT THE WORLD — "harness '<x>' is not registered in the harness registry" — whose own advice is to go register it (a WRITE, i.e. actionable in the wrong direction); (4) `plans/list.ts:549` regex-matches that message and swallows it into `unknownHarnesses`, returning ok:true + []. `host-benign-errors.ts:141-159` also marks it benign, so it never raises the error rate — invisible in telemetry too. FIX (structural, not detection): give `resolveWorkspaceForHarnessSlugIn` a discriminated verdict (found | absent | unreadable-with-cause) instead of one `null`; let `resolvePlanScope` assert "not registered" ONLY after a read that genuinely SUCCEEDED and returned no row; make list.ts's swallow key off that typed verdict rather than a regex over an error string; drop the fault variant from the benign classifier. Note the general rule this earns: an error-STRING match can never separate a real absence from a fault that renders the same words — the distinction must be typed at the source. Testable without a live DB via the existing injectable seams (`resolvePlanScope`'s `registryFallback`, `fill_workspace_id_from_projects`'s `lookup`): inject a throwing `loadHarnessRegistry` and assert plans:list does NOT answer ok:true/[] for a harness whose rows are present.  — note: ← WI-2141821 completed (done)

items.text: Fleet rosters report present state only, so a fleet that LOST 10 members reads as a healthy 1-member fleet (WI-7130) — and this does not merely hide loss, it FABRICATES a phantom event. A dead member drops out of the roster, so `summary.dead: 0` was literally true and completely misleading; the only alert raised was about the leader sitting idle. A monitor loop calls this tool every wake BY DESIGN, so the one question a monitor most needs — did I lose anyone — is the one its own tool cannot ask. Worse: because loss is discovered late and all at once, BATCHED DISCOVERY IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A BATCHED EVENT. That is what put "mass death" in the leader's head before a single timestamp was read, and it aimed two successive hypotheses at a simultaneous killer that never existed. Fix is a read, not new bookkeeping: `membersLost: N, since: <ts>` from the already-recorded ended_at.  — note: ← WI-2141824 completed (done)

items.text: Build the DEGENERATE-WAKE detector (WI-7129, re-keyed — see the REJECTED mass-death decision). Agents do not get killed; they degenerate into telemetry-only wake loops and quietly run down. Measured on the 8 dead members: final-30-min mix of 254 calls/205 telemetry/3 work, 226/177/6, 216/166/10, 147/116/1 — and all 8 ended on the identical `coord:glance`+`activity:report`+`flags:get` triple within one second, 7.5k-9k calls deep. Nothing catches it because a burning agent is heartbeat-fresh, present and `sessionState:"live"` right up to the moment it stops: it is spending real tokens to report that it is fine. Signal: per agent over a trailing window (~30 min, >=40 calls), telemetry_ratio > ~0.75 AND work_calls <= ~5 — fires at 0.79-0.81 on that cohort well before they stopped. Calibrate against a healthy cohort first. The root-cause fix is EI-19307414464301772; build the detector anyway, the class will recur under another mechanism.  — note: ← WI-2141825 done

items.text: No base-rate primitive: every read is a FILTERED read with no denominator, so ordinary variation reads as an anomaly (EI-19375528138828761). Agents reason forward from a cluster without ever testing whether the cluster is remarkable. On 2026-08-02 this produced two wrong answers and a near-miss third: the investigation was dissolved by one flat minute-histogram, and a "24h lifetime cap" (7 chains at 23.8-24.1h, start/stop positively correlated) was refuted by the same table returning chains of 32/66/111/166/193h. Both times the suggestive cluster and its refutation were seconds apart in one relation. Fix, in preference order: (1) denominator-in-result — when a tool returns a filtered slice of a countable population, include the population size and window ("matched 8 of 392 sessions in this window"); (2) a `baseline:compare` verb returning a metric over trailing comparable windows. Not another detector — a habit-forming default.  — note: ← WI-2141826 completed (done)

items.text: No tool answers "what cgroup/scope is this agent in" — the question that decides what can kill it (WI-7134). Diagnosis required shelling into /proc, and `pgrep -f <ownerId>` SELF-MATCHED the agent's own command line on three of four lookups, returning the caller's pid as if it were the target's — a silent wrong answer of exactly this plan's shape, and the same family as the documented `pkill -f` self-match trap. Fix: expose the agent's cgroup path / transient scope on an existing presence or process surface (`processes:list` already carries provenance), so "what confines this agent" is a read rather than a shell excursion using a known-defective idiom. — note: ← WI-2141828 completed (done)

items.text: Keep observation-grade captures OUT of the claimable pool: route them to the observation lane at FILING time, and exclude nit-severity auto-filed items from the default claim floors. This is the ROOT CAUSE — the count only misleads because the pool is full of things that are not work. [WI-6675]  — note: Applying D-114, whose ruling was recorded but never executed on the item. D-114 measured P-008's root-cause premise FALSE at census: observation routing already works (99.4% of nit-grade captures already in lane='observation', routed by DECLARED INTENT via the explicit improvements:capture opt-in), so there was no filing-hygiene defect to fix. Fix: either accept `projection` generically at the door, or narrow the advertisement to the tools that actually declare it.  — note: ← WI-2141829 completed (done)

items.text: OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-07-03 (aviynw6) — SU/fleet AUTO = ZERO owner-confirm pauses. Strip the confirm-with-owner / owner-authority gating language from the SU AUTO clause in operating-modes-policy.ts (renderModesPolicy, full + fleet tiers) + any tool guidance telling SU to confirm, so an autonomously-operating SU session NEVER pauses to ask the owner — even for genuinely irreversible / outward-facing / destructive / privilege-escalation actions: PROCEED and DISCLOSE (the disposition/report path), never gate. items.text: Bound concurrent affected-sweeps and make their verdict durable (EI-18699972365875475). Measured: 17 concurrent `affected-tests.mjs` sweeps at loadavg 137.8. Mechanism — every agent runs `test:affected` as CLAUDE.md instructs, nothing serializes them, each fans out to many vitest workers, so N agents produce N full fan-outs (multiplicative, not additive). This is a correctness hazard rather than mere slowness: sweep duration outliving a session boundary converted a PASSING run into an unreadable one (native `run_in_background` bookkeeping dies on respawn, EI-16611) and blocked a 7-item plan's last lane on a verdict that already existed. Add a concurrency cap with queueing reusing `scripts/lib/fs-mutex.mjs`, and make the durable log path the ADVERTISED way to read a verdict.  — note: DROPPED — premise was wrong and I retracted it. Both halves already exist and work; my measurement was a miscount.

items.text: Serve the /vditor/** mirror with `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` (host-spa.ts serveFile). Found during P-006: unpkg was sending max-age=31536000 and we sent NO cache headers at all, so the local mirror won the COLD fetch (~30ms vs ~225ms) but lost the WARM one (~30ms vs ~4ms) — serveFile readFileSync's all 3.9MB per page load. The mirror is a wholesale copy of one PINNED version, replaced not mutated on upgrade, so `immutable` is safe. Verified on :3170 after a restart: header present on /vditor/*, absent on /favicon.ico.

items.text: papercusp-authority-rpc-signed (security hardening — ON is the MORE-secure state). ON effect: POST /api/authority/rpc REQUIRES a valid Ed25519-signed caller envelope before a mutating lock/claim op. VERIFY: (1) a validly-signed envelope is accepted; (2) an UNSIGNED or forged-sig envelope is REJECTED (the security property — closes the self-reported-holderPubkey hole); (3) on a box where every peer runs current code (the transport always signs), NO valid caller is rejected. Cross-machine: confirm no false rejections across real peers running current code. PASS = forged rejected + valid accepted + zero false-rejects. Risk if wrong: valid authority RPCs rejected (lock ops fail-open → double-grants) OR forged accepted (security hole).  (VERIFIED PASS — see D-003. Live :3070 rejected unsigned envelope unauthenticated; 47/47 tests; transport always signs.) (← WI-1068 completed) (← WI-1068 completed)

items.text: papercusp-substrate-sidecar (owner flipped ON 2026-06-29 to test). ON effect: bootAllHarnessesForActiveWorkspace spawns a dedicated sidecar process (apps/operator/bin/substrate-sidecar.ts, JSON-RPC 2.0 over a Unix socket) that owns the corestores / Hyperswarm natives / merge loops / replication, freeing the main operator (:3070) from GC pauses + per-harness RSS. BOOT-SCOPED: read once at boot, so a RESTART is required for the flip to take effect. Gated on: Phase 1/2 incomplete + "never :3070 until integration-verified" (two-peer-swarm federation test + event-loop-latency regression test). KNOWN BLOCKER to confirm: Corestore 7.x holds a process-level RocksDB file lock per storage path, so the main process + sidecar cannot both open the store — the wrapper is documented to spawn the sidecar then FALL BACK to in-process. VERIFY: (1) after restart, does the substrate actually run IN the sidecar, or does it fall back in-process? (check boot logs for the sidecar spawn + whether it serves replication or logs the fallback); (2) IF it runs in the sidecar: confirm two-peer federation still works through it AND measure the event-loop-latency improvement on the main process (the whole point of the offload), with no federation regression; (3) IF it falls back: that confirms the RocksDB-lock blocker is still open — report it as the gating issue (the real fix is a separate-storage-path / true out-of-process design). PASS = sidecar serves replication without falling back AND federation + main-process latency improve with no regression. FAIL/BLOCKED = falls back in-process (expected today). Risk if the fallback is not clean: substrate boot disruption on restart.  (VERIFIED PASS D-007 — runs IN the sidecar live pid 2362608, federation works peer_connected, NO fallback. Better than the brief's expected-fallback. Minor follow-ups: latency A/B + MaxListeners cleanup.) (← WI-1072 completed) (← WI-1072 completed)

items.text: Promoter routine: tier:durable, every 30 min, NOT an agent spawn. Verdicts: PROMOTE / MERGE into canonical (see_also + reporter fold + close superseded-with-pointer) / HOLD-escalate. CHARTER HARD RULE: duplication only, never merit (kappa 0.679 vs 0.289). Verdict rows carry model id + config. Check work_items:judge_redundancy / set_redundancy / promote tool semantics FIRST and extend rather than rebuild. VERIFY: replay the six vitest clones through the gate — one promotes, five merge; an R-remedy pair both promote, linked.  — note: ← WI-41384 completed (done)

items.text: Promoter routine: tier:durable, every 30 min, NOT an agent spawn. Per tick: fetch pending batch (~20); exact checks (watchdogKey/conditionKey, normalized title); embedding top-K neighbors over open AND recently-terminal items (catches restates-already-closed, the audit's one surviving filter at 65-75% precision); batch-internal comparison; zero-flag items PROMOTE with no model call; flagged pairs to ONE batched strong-model call with the D-025/D-027 R-finding/R-remedy/R-related code set. Verdicts: PROMOTE / MERGE into canonical (see_also + reporter fold + close superseded-with-pointer) / HOLD-escalate. CHARTER HARD RULE: duplication only, never merit (kappa 0.679 vs 0.289). Verdict rows carry model id + config. Check work_items:judge_redundancy / set_redundancy / promote tool semantics FIRST and extend rather than rebuild. VERIFY: replay the six vitest clones through the gate — one promotes, five merge; an R-remedy pair both promote, linked.  — note: ← WI-41384 completed (done)

items.text: Promoter routine: tier:durable, every 30 min, NOT an agent spawn. Per tick: fetch pending batch (~20); exact checks (watchdogKey/conditionKey, normalized title); embedding top-K neighbors over open AND recently-terminal items (catches restates-already-closed, the audit's one surviving filter at 65-75% precision); batch-internal comparison; zero-flag items PROMOTE with no model call; flagged pairs to ONE batched strong-model call with the D-025/D-027 R-finding/R-remedy/R-related code set. Verdicts: PROMOTE / MERGE into canonical (see_also + reporter fold + close superseded-with-pointer) / HOLD-escalate. CHARTER HARD RULE: duplication only, never merit (kappa 0.679 vs 0.289). Verdict rows carry model id + config. Check work_items:judge_redundancy / set_redundancy / promote tool semantics FIRST and extend rather than rebuild. VERIFY: replay the six vitest clones through the gate — one promotes, five merge; an R-remedy pair both promote, linked.  — note: ← WI-41384 completed (done)

Verdicts: PROMOTE / MERGE into canonical (see_also + reporter fold + close superseded-with-pointer) / HOLD-escalate. CHARTER HARD RULE: duplication only, never merit (kappa 0.679 vs 0.289). Verdict rows carry model id + config. Check work_items:judge_redundancy / set_redundancy / promote tool semantics FIRST and extend rather than rebuild. VERIFY: replay the six vitest clones through the gate — one promotes, five merge; an R-remedy pair both promote, linked.  — note: ← WI-41384 completed (done)
